Accomplishments: Completed Release 8.3.14 Operational Readiness Review and Transition to Operations. Completed Release 8.3.15 Implementation. Implementation Metrics: Added 15.38 M new catalog files to the archive.  Operational Availability: 98.86%. The investment is executing as expected.

The Geographic Support Program (GSP) investment supports the integrated and automated computer-based geographic support system crucial to all censuses and household surveys. The investment continues to provide the Census address list, maps, geographic reference files, and processing systems to meet the geographic requirements of all Census Bureau programs and operations. Census counts on GSP to be able to accurately locate people and places for data collection. Accomplishments: Delivered Address Data Dump to the Listing and Mapping Application (LiMA). Delivered Boundary and Annexation Survey 2026 production pipe-delimited state-based Master Address File Extract (MAFX), MAF Operation Codes Files (MAFOP) & tally files to the Enterprise Data Lake (EDL). Began conducting Interactive Spatial, T13 & Auto QC of the TIGERweb Geodatabase. This activity is currently in the process of being completed as of 1/7/2026. The Investment is progressing with some risk exposure that is being mitigated.

The Central Processing investment continues to provide increased satellite network bandwidth, processing and storage capacity. It collects, communicates, processes, displays, and analyzes hydro-meteorological data that supports the NWS mission of accurate forecasts/warnings. Accomplishments: WCOSS: Continue transition of Interactive Multi-sensor Snow and Ice Mapping System (IMS) application in support of National Ice Center. NAWIPS: Down-select meeting took place in December to narrow down vendors to continue through acquisition process. AWIPS: Network Availability: 100%. Satellite Master Ground Station Availability: 100%. Investment is rated a 3 due to risk profile and issues.

Enterprise Data Lake continues to be a flexible data repository intended to provide the Census Bureau with a next generation scaling capability to fulfill data storage, reporting, analytics, and security needs while reducing costs associated with duplicative data silos. Notable Accomplishments: DEMO: Delivered Demo DevSecOps and DSD Frames and Sampling UAT Environment. Decennial: Completed cross-account access for requested ADDCP systems and analyst projects that require access to Mojo Prod Iceberg tables. Delivered InOE Project: Adrec Quality ITE Additional Production EC2 for Quantum. Addressed adhoc request and identified issues in the designated trackers for all systems and projects onboarded to EDL. ECON: Delivered RolesAnywhere for ABS SIF delivery.  The investment is rated 3 due to risk exposure and reporting concerns.

The 2030 Decennial investment covers the Design Selection Phase (FYs 2022 - 2024) for the 2030 Census.  The 2030 Census strategic goals are consistent with prior decennial census goals and include: 1) A Complete and Accurate Census, 2) Embraced and Trusted Results, 3) An Efficient and Effective Program, and 4) An Appropriately Sized, Skilled, and Structured Workforce. This investment is currently in the Design Selection Phase for the 2030 Census and is on target to meet all scheduled milestones. Accomplishments:  2026 Census Test: 26CT IT Systems that are not already conducting operations, continue to make progress towards development and integration resting milestones. Completed the development, design, and implementation of system changes necessary to integrate USPS personnel as part of the 26 Census test field hiring. 2028 Dress Rehearsal: Completed the 2028 Systems high-level architecture design for the first operation deliverable for non traditional living quarters. The investment is rated a 3 - medium risk due to increased risks associated with the design phase of the Decennial.

investmentName: Census - Data Ingest and Collection for the Enterprise (DICE)
comment: The Data Ingest and Collection for the Enterprise (DICE) investment continues with implementing a new way of doing business that focuses on minimizing redundancy, lowering complexity, and avoiding duplicative costs for the Census's business and household data ingest and collection operations. DICE continues the efforts of being able to provide a way to collect quality data using one source. The program also continues its efforts to integrate and manage the development of an enterprise system that provides a shared platform for receiving data that has been collected by external sources, census, and survey data. Accomplishments: Special Census 2025 - West Des Moines, IA - DICE Activities Complete 12/12/25. Investment is improving in reporting and is progressing in execution but is operating with risk exposure.

investmentName: BIS Commerce USXPORTS Exporter Support System (CUESS)
comment: The BIS CUESS investment complements the export enforcement process in support of the single IT System for the Export Control Reform directive. BIS continues to collaborate with other agencies on the USXPORTS system for multi-agency license reviews and actively transmitting referral data. BIS continues to support the USXPORTS development for releases that improve the reliability and data efficiencies between CUESS and USXPORTS. BIS and the State Department continue to share data weekly in support of the recommendation from the GAO. Accomplishments: SNAP-R Hardening: Supported users with migration challenges and questions on new SNAP-R interface. OICTS Compliance Application and Reporting System (CARS): Completed and released to production for trusted entities association setup process, enabling external partners to submit on behalf of regulated parties, UAS third party information and UAS audit report. O&M: Implemented eight maintenance change requests: multiple updates on IMSR end use check, allow searching by approver of IMSR screen review, added new LOA FACT code, transferred RWA no-referral cases to USXPORTS, delete IMSR actions and activities that were mistakenly created, preserve the comment created dates when converting IMSR case to lead, fix issue on IMSR search and make ECCN and dollar values required when approving detention and seizure actions  Investment is progressing with risks.

investmentName: Census - Center for Enterprise Dissemination Services and Consumer Information (CEDSCI).
comment: The Program and the CEDSCI EDDE IT Platform project continues to be dedicated to using customer feedback to develop innovative ways to improve customer with improved data and product displays, searches, and downloads accessible from census.gov and on mobile devices. The project is in the development of a modernized platform that disseminates Census data in an efficient technological manner.  The program is responsible for both the development project plus using the new platform for disseminating Census data.  Notable Accomplishments: Releases to data.census.gov including 2023 ECNSVY Module Characteristics of Businesses, 2022 GEO Geography Information, 2022 ECNSVY Company Summary, 2022 ECN Construction: Value of Business Done for Kind-of-Business, 2022 ECN Construction: Value of Construction Work for Location of Construction Work for U.S. and States, 2021 GEO Geography Information, Timeseries PUB Public Sector Annual Surveys and Census of Governments, Timeseries SOMA Survey of Market Absorption, Timeseries IDB Time Series International Database: International Populations by Single year of Age and Sex, Timeseries IDB Time Series International Database 5-Year Age Groups and Sex and Other Demographic Variables. The investment continues to have a risk exposure contributing to the overall rating.

investmentName: NOAA/OCIO/ NOAA R&D High Performance Computing System (HPCS)
comment: HPCS continues to be a constellation of super computers used by NOAA to perform research and development to improve climate and weather models that is meeting the mission requirements in performance.  The HPCS investment is in Operational and Maintenance mode and consistently meets and exceeds performance metrics. Accomplishments: Outside Pad construction at NESCC complete to allow compute installation to begin System availability 99.62%; Data availability 100%; Compute hours made available 676,439,175. The American Community Survey has led to a simpler decennial census, provided more timely and relevant data between censuses, and led to widespread efficiencies throughout the federal statistical system. Notable accomplishment: Completed Deliver 1-Year Webinar for 1Year_DataRelease_DY2024. Completed 2026 GQ CAPI Verification Test. The investment is progressing as expected.

investmentName: FAAXX740: Regulation and Certification Infrastructure for System Safety (RCISS)
comment: For the month of September, the Regulation and Certification Infrastructure for System Safety (RCISS) Investment has a Low Risk Rating. The RCISS program has deployed 51 of the 55 telecommunication switches at the Aviation Safety (AVS) field sites. The completion of the deployments are scheduled to complete in September 2025.

For the month of September, the Voice Communications Systems (VCS) Investment remains at a Moderately Low Risk Rating. The VCS program completed Key Site installations at Southern California TRACON (SCT) and Indianapolis Air Route Traffic Control Center (ZID) in August 2025 for Air-to-Ground Protocol Converter (APC) systems.

For the month of September, the Common Support Services Weather (CSS-Wx) Investment remains at a Moderately Low Risk Rating. Several missed key milestones, including the Independent Operational Assessment (IOA), In-Service Decision (ISD), and the First-Site Operational Readiness Date (ORD), are now scheduled for first quarter of calendar year 2026. The Last-Site ORD originally scheduled for April 2026 is at risk due to the delay of the IOA and ISD.

For the month of September, the Data Communications NextGen Support (DataComm) Investment remains at a High Risk Rating. The deployment of Full Services (FS) Increment 2 has started. Increment 2 is now scheduled to complete First-Site Initial Operational Capability (IOC) in November 2025. The program is projecting a $12.1M cost increase and has updated its expected completion date for Last Site IOC to July 2027.

For the month of September, the Runway Status Lights (RWSL) Investment remains at a Moderately Low Risk Rating. RWSL met or exceeded 100% of the operational performance targets for all five of its monthly operational metrics.

For the month of September, the Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) Investment remains at a Medium Risk Rating. For the ADS-B Enhancement program, an updated Initial Service Acceptance Test (ISAT) Report for Service Volume 331 (Upper Yukon River) was completed for the ADS-B Service Expansion in Alaska. The ADS-B Future Segments program is still experiencing milestone delays due to unmet test requirements, performance issues and software development delays.

For the month of September, the System Wide Information Management (SWIM) Investment remains at a Medium Risk Rating. The SWIM Segment 2C program is projecting a one-month delay in the last milestone, ‘Complete Deployment of SWIM Terminal Data Distribution Service (STDDS) R6.1’ and the ‘Store and Forward Application (SAFA) Deployment’, due to Time Division Multiplexing (TDM) / Internet Protocol (IP) Infrastructure Replacement. The deployment of STDDS has completed 37 sites out of 38 and the SAFA deployments have completed 130 of the 141 sites  All remaining SWIM Segment 2D milestones will be missed due to the FAA Enterprise Network Services (FENS) replan. A pathway forward for the SWIM Segment 2D program is currently under review.

For the month of September, the Traffic Flow Management System (TFMS) Investment remains at a Moderately Low Risk Rating. TFMS coordination meetings, stakeholder engagement sessions, and detailed deployment step reviews have been scheduled in preparation for the ‘Night of Deployment’ in September 2025.

investmentName: FAAXX612: System Approach for Safety Oversight (SASO)
comment: For the month of September, the System Approach for Safety Oversight (SASO) Investment remains at a Moderately Low Risk Rating. The SASO program continues to stay on schedule with no major risks to report.

investmentName: FAAXX610: Aviation Safety Knowledge Management Environment (ASKME)
comment: For the month of September, the Aviation Safety Knowledge Management Environment (ASKME) Investment remains at a Moderately Low Risk Rating. The ASKME program completed User Acceptance Testing (UAT)  for Appian Enablement Services and Palantir Enablement Services in August 2025.

For the month of September, the Time-Based Flow Management (TBFM) Investment remains at a Moderately Low Risk Rating. TBFM future milestones may be at risk due to issues found in hardware components and lack of training resources. Miami (ZMA) Key Site is planned for September 2025 and is on track for completion.

investmentName: FAAXX600: Oceanic Automation System: Advanced Technologies and Oceanic Procedures (ATOP)
comment: For the month of September, the Oceanic Automation System: Advanced Technologies and Oceanic Procedures (ATOP) Investment remains at a Medium Risk Rating. The ATOP Enhancement 1 (E1) Release T32 Initial Operational Capability (IOC) at the First-Site is now scheduled for completion in September 2026. The Sustainment 3 Phase 1 program remains on schedule with no current risks to major milestone completion.  ​

For the month of September, the ERAM Enhancement and Sustainment Investment remains at a Medium Risk Rating. Enhancement 2 & Sustainment 3 continue to have milestones behind schedule. ERAM Sustainment 3 (ES3) introduced a third deployment team which has helped reduce the schedule impact from 10 months to seven months. ERAM Operating System (OS) Upgrade major milestones continue to stay on schedule with no risks being reported to milestone completion.

For the month of September, the En Route Automation Modernization (ERAM) Investment has a Moderately Low Risk Rating. ERAM met or exceeded 100% of the operational performance targets for all six of its monthly operational metrics.
For the month of September, the NextGen R&D Portfolio Investment remains at a Moderately Low Risk Rating. Discussions are ongoing regarding the next steps for the CSS-FD program.

For the month of September, the NextGen Weather (Wx) Processor (NWP) Investment remains at a Moderately Low Risk Rating. The First-site Operational Readiness Date (ORD) is still projected for September 2025. The Program expects delays with the Independent Operational Assessment (IOA) which has been rescheduled for early 2026.

For the month of September, the Next Generation Air/Ground Communications (NEXCOM) Investment remains at a Moderately Low Risk Rating, the cost variance for NEXCOM Phase 2 is reporting a -6% variance because of a $19M cost increase.

investmentName: FAAXX748: Weather Sensors Technology Refresh Portfolio (WSTRP)
comment: For the month of September, the Weather Sensors Technology Refresh Portfolio (WSTRP) Investment remains at a Moderately Low Risk Rating. Milestones continue to complete as baselined.

For the month of September, the Terminal Primary Surveillance (TPS) Investment remains at a Medium Risk Rating due to potential schedule delays with the Airport Surveillance Radar (ASR) Model 9 (ASR-9) Sustainment 3 program. ​For ASR-8 Sustainment 1, several projects are being re-evaluated or paused because of the Radar Modernization effort.​

For the month of September, the Instrument Flight Procedures Automation (IFPA) Investment remains at a Moderately Low Risk Rating. ​Due to new fund request requirements increasing the length of time to receive approval and close contracts, there are now schedule concerns for the IFPA Sustainment 3 remaining projects. If there is a lack of funding or delay due to this process, it would create negative impacts to project schedules.

For the month of September, the Terminal Flight Data Manager (TFDM) Investment remains at a Moderately High Risk Rating. The Initial Operational Capability (IOC) was achieved for San Francisco (SFO) and Build 2 has been deployed. All nine remaining Build 1 sites will now begin to be upleveled to Build 2.

For the month of September, the Enterprise Information Display System (E-IDS) Investment is Moderately Low Risk. Under the new streamlined review process to meet project schedules, Plan Expedite combines previous Project Phases 1 and 2 where the full deployment will be achieved in three years (by the end of fiscal year 2028). The Project Scope now includes 435 sites vice 23 sites.

investmentName: FAAXX159: Voice Switching and Control System (VSCS)
comment: For the month of September, the Voice Switching and Control System (VSCS) Investment remains at a Low Risk Rating. The VSCS Sustainment Phase 4 program successfully completed the Baseline Product Review (BPR)  in August 2025 for the Common Switch Power Supply (CSPS). Performance metrics continue to be reported on time and targeted goals are being met.

investmentName: FAAXX164: Standard Terminal Automation Replacement System (STARS)
comment: For the month of September, the Standard Terminal Automation Replacement System (STARS) Investment remains at a Medium Risk Rating. For STARS Sustainment 3, there are now 34 operational FAA sites using the Linux Operating System. For the STARS Sustainment 4 program, progress continues towards completion of the next major milestone.​

For the month of September, the Offshore Automation (OA) Investment is at a Moderately Low Risk Rating. The next milestone, ‘Complete Systems Engineering on OA Functionality for Anchorage (ZAN) Air Route Traffic Control Center (ARTCC)’, is projected to complete in October 2025, eight months past the baselined date.

For the month of September, the Wide Area Augmentation System (WAAS) Investment remains at a Moderately Low Risk Rating. Schedule delays, up to 21 months are possible, due to contractor performance, loss of experienced personnel over the last two years, and technical difficulties associated with the integration of new processors and the migration from the AIX operating system to the Linux operating system.

investmentName: FAAXX171: FAA Enterprise Network Services (FENS) (Formerly FTI-2)
comment: For the month of September, the FAA Enterprise Network Services (FENS) Investment remains at a Medium Risk Rating. The FENS program continues to replan to accommodate Time Division Multiplexing (TDM) / Internet Protocol (IP) related migration challenges. The FENS program is also evaluating how to support the telecommunication modernization effort.

For the month of September, the Airport Surface Detection Equipment (ASDE) Investment remains at a Moderately Low Risk Rating. Monthly performance metrics continued to be reported on time. The next milestone, ‘Surface Movement Radars (SMR) Infrastructure Service Life Extension Program (SLEP) – Complete Remote Tower Painting’, is projected to complete in September 2025.

For the month of September, the FAA Telecommunications Infrastructure (FTI) Investment remains at a Moderately Low Risk Rating. FTI achieved an on-time service delivery rate of 99.56% during August 2025. As a result, the overall on-time service delivery for the past 12 months increased slightly from 99.5% to 99.7%. All 5 RMA levels for FTI telecommunication services supporting NAS Operations are being met in the aggregate.

investmentName: Census - Data Ingest and Collection for the Enterprise (DICE)
comment: The Data Ingest and Collection for the Enterprise (DICE) investment continues with implementing a new way of doing business that focuses on minimizing redundancy, lowering complexity, and avoiding duplicative costs for the Census's business and household data ingest and collection operations. DICE continues the efforts of being able to provide a way to collect quality data using one source. The program also continues its efforts to integrate and manage the development of an enterprise system that provides a shared platform for receiving data that has been collected by external sources, census, and survey data. Accomplishments: Integration Testing began: Integration testing for the field test began on August 6, 2025. Activities for the Data Ingest and Collection for the Enterprise (DICE) were completed on August 19, 2025. investmentName: Census - Center for Enterprise Dissemination Services and Consumer Information (CEDSCI).
comment: The Program and the CEDSCI EDDE IT Platform project continues to be dedicated to using customer feedback to develop innovative ways to improve customer with improved data and product displays, searches, and downloads accessible from census.gov and on mobile devices. The project is in the development of a modernized platform that disseminates Census data in an efficient technological manner.  The program is responsible for both the development project plus using the new platform for disseminating Census data.  Notable Accomplishments: CEDSCI successfully released 26 datasets in August including 22 of American Housing Survey (AHS) which totaled 1.5TB of data - one of the largest data releases in our program's history. Progress continued on the migration to cloud, the transition from Elasticsearch to OpenSearch, and the shift from Jenkins to GitLab. UI improvements and mobile responsiveness efforts advanced for MDAT, along with enhancements to the open code Aqua library components. In addition, An Address Search widget was developed to enable usage on Census.gov. Several defects were also resolved across both Data.census.gov and MDAT.  The investment continues to have a risk exposure contributing to the overall rating.

comment: TraCSS is the Department of Commerce's enterprise solution civil space traffic coordination investment to meet Space Policy Directive 3 issued in 2018. comment: TraCSS is the Department of Commerce's enterprise solution civil space traffic coordination investment to meet Space Policy Directive 3 issued in 2018.  Directive 3 designates the Department of Commerce as the lead civilian agency for providing basic SSA data and STM services to commercial space operators.  On behalf of DOC, NOAA's Office of Space Commerce is developing the Traffic Coordination System for Space TraCSS. TraCSS will ingest, archive, process, and disseminate Space Situational Awareness (SSA) data and products for space safety and sustainability and provide conjunction analysis and warning services to commercial satellite owner/operators. Accomplishments: Updating program integrated schedule to reflect presentation layer protest impacts.  The investment is rated a 3 due to increased risks.

The American Community Survey (ACS) Investment continues to support the Bureau's objective of collecting, processing, and releasing information to meet the constitutional and legislative mandates. The American Community Survey has led to a simpler decennial census, provided more timely and relevant data between censuses, and led to widespread efficiencies throughout the federal statistical system. Notable accomplishment: Uploaded Web Info Copies for HUSR_2024OM_2025_Development. Completed Content Review for ACS_GQ_2025. Completed the 5 Year Data Release DY2023 Comparison Guidance Webpage. Completed the 5 Year Table Change Webpage for 5 Year Data Release DY2023. The investment is progressing as expected.

The Geographic Support Program (GSP) investment supports the integrated and automated computer-based geographic support system crucial to all censuses and household surveys. The investment continues to provide the Census address list, maps, geographic reference files, and processing systems to meet the geographic requirements of all Census Bureau programs and operations. Census counts on GSP to be able to accurately locate people and places for data collection. Accomplishments: This month GSP continued to be successful in providing updates by completing the targeted delivery sequences file refresh, including preprocessing and quality control. Additionally, GSP processed the Parcel and Address Matching Master Address Files update. The Investment is progressing with some risk exposure that is being mitigated.

investmentName: Census - Center for Enterprise Dissemination Services and Consumer Information (CEDSCI).
comment: The Program and the CEDSCI EDDE IT Platform project continues to be dedicated to using customer feedback to develop innovative ways to improve customer with improved data and product displays, searches, and downloads accessible from census.gov and on mobile devices. The project is in the development of a modernized platform that disseminates Census data in an efficient technological manner.  The program is responsible for both the development project plus using the new platform for disseminating Census data.  Notable Accomplishments: CEDSCI developed key features for Phase 1 of the My Tribal Area app. CEDSCI improved usability and mobile responsiveness of data.census.gov and the MDAT application. Additionally, CEDSCI advanced the Wayfinder app proof of concept that provides an intuitive interface for access to on-demand Census API data. They added performance enhancements to tables, maps, charts, MDAT, and the Population Pyramid app. Completed Phase O of the Cloud migration activity to begin to set-up developer accounts.  The investment continues to have a risk exposure contributing to the overall rating.

The 2030 Decennial investment covers the Design Selection Phase (FYs 2022 - 2024) for the 2030 Census.  The 2030 Census strategic goals are consistent with prior decennial census goals and include: 1) A Complete and Accurate Census, 2) Embraced and Trusted Results, 3) An Efficient and Effective Program, and 4) An Appropriately Sized, Skilled, and Structured Workforce. This investment is currently in the Design Selection Phase for the 2030 Census and is on target to meet all scheduled milestones. The investment is rated a 3 - medium risk due to increased risks associated with the design phase of the Decennial.

comment: TraCSS is the Department of Commerce's enterprise solution civil space traffic coordination investment to meet Space Policy Directive 3 issued in 2018. TraCSS will ingest, archive, process, and disseminate Space Situational Awareness (SSA) data and products for space safety and sustainability and provide conjunction analysis and warning services to commercial satellite owner/operators. comment: The CLASS program continues to efficiently manage high volumes (petabytes) of satellite and in situ data and automates data ingest, quality control and access. CLASS is the designated primary archive for most of the NOAA environmental data sets. CLASS is providing knowledge transfer to NCCF to ensure CLASS capabilities are understood. The investment is executing as expected.

The American Community Survey has led to a simpler decennial census, provided more timely and relevant data between censuses, and led to widespread efficiencies throughout the federal statistical system. Notable accomplishment: Completed posting the PUMS User Guide documents to PUMS Documentation Website for 5 Year PUMS DY23. Completed posting code lists & subject list to the FTP site for 5 Year PUMS DY23. Completed posting PUMS ReadMe document to the FTP site for 5 Year PUMS DY23. OneNWS Network Availability: 100%. NWR Transmitter Availability: 97.80%. The investment is rated a 3 due to the risk profile and issues.

The investment continues to provide the Census address list, maps, geographic reference files, and processing systems to meet the geographic requirements of all Census Bureau programs and operations. Census counts on GSP to be able to accurately locate people and places for data collection. Accomplishments: This month GSP continues to provide master address test files along with Test SAS Geographic Reference files.  Delivered Address Data Dump to the Listing and Mapping Application (LiMA). The Investment is progressing with some risk exposure that is being mitigated.

The 2030 Decennial investment covers the Design Selection Phase (FYs 2022 - 2024) for the 2030 Census.  The 2030 Census strategic goals are consistent with prior decennial census goals and include: 1) A Complete and Accurate Census, 2) Embraced and Trusted Results, 3) An Efficient and Effective Program, and 4) An Appropriately Sized, Skilled, and Structured Workforce. This investment is currently in the Design Selection Phase for the 2030 Census and is on target to meet all scheduled milestones. Accomplishments: Integrated Baseline Reviews (IBRs) were completed for four operational delivery areas: Selection, Hiring, Self-Response and In-Office Enumeration. The investment is rated a 3 - medium risk due to increased risks associated with the design phase of the Decennial.

They fixed 22 defects from UAT and deployed all modules to production with continued UAT planned. investmentName: Census - Data Ingest and Collection for the Enterprise (DICE)
comment: The Data Ingest and Collection for the Enterprise (DICE) investment continues with implementing a new way of doing business that focuses on minimizing redundancy, lowering complexity, and avoiding duplicative costs for the Census's business and household data ingest and collection operations. DICE continues the efforts of being able to provide a way to collect quality data using one source. The program also continues its efforts to integrate and manage the development of an enterprise system that provides a shared platform for receiving data that has been collected by external sources, census, and survey data. Accomplishments: New functionality added to QDM that was recently provided from Centurion to "create a new unit" when coming back for the 2nd+ attempts (12/17/24). The Translations Office delivered a Spanish version of the CPS screen content to the QDM team on 12/6. AIES-24: Updated testing content delivered following the QDM 12/18/24 sprint release (12/19) and eCORR sprint release 16.4 (12/20). Special Census: Ankeny, IA; Bondurant, IA; Columbia, TN; Polk City, IA; McDonough County, IL; Urbana, IL -Cases complete.  Investment is improving in reporting and is progressing in execution but is operating with risk exposure.

Decommissioned all 3 RDS instances, allowing Project to switch over to Aurora serverless full time. OCC/LLM: Delivered ITE workspace to customer. LakeFront: EDC multi-account migration code deployment to Core Dev environment for both Front End and Back End was successfully completed. comment: TraCSS is the Department of Commerce's enterprise solution civil space traffic coordination investment to meet Space Policy Directive 3 issued in 2018.  Directive 3 designates the Department of Commerce as the lead civilian agency for providing basic SSA data and STM services to commercial space operators.  On behalf of DOC, NOAA's Office of Space Commerce is developing the Traffic Coordination System for Space TraCSS. TraCSS will ingest, archive, process, and disseminate Space Situational Awareness (SSA) data and products for space safety and sustainability and will provide conjunction analysis and warning services to commercial satellite owner/operators. Accomplishments: Resolved outstanding beta test anomalies. Engaging with beta users to continue robust system assessment. Held Industry Day for TraCSS System Integrator 2.0. Hired Cost Estimator. Awarded presentation layer contract as planned. The investment is rated a 4 due to successful MVP deployment and continuing favorable results in beta evaluation.

investmentName: NOAA/OCIO/ NOAA R&D High Performance Computing System (HPCS)
comment: HPCS continues to be a constellation of super computers used by NOAA to perform research and development to improve climate and weather models that is meeting the mission requirements in performance.  The HPCS investment is in Operational and Maintenance mode and consistently meets and exceeds performance metrics. Accomplishments: System availability 99.18%; Data availability 100%; Compute hours made available 557,214,336. Large increase to NOAA Enterprise HPC Compute in FY25 without supporting O&M funding that is impacted by $20M reduction in FY 2024 and possible hard earmark to program further impacting future capacity. Progressing with risk and issues on capacity impacting the rating.

The Economic Censuses and Surveys program is a mixed life cycle investment and continues to support statistical programs that count and profile U.S. businesses and government organizations. ECON investment accomplishments include: The DIPSE Redesign Team completed testing and bug fixes for the Coverage Change Request Tool. They performed updates to test automation for the new reference period and began testing Enterprise and Establishment Add Prior Prior Year modules. The AIES/SPACE team successfully provisioned Aurora databases across DEV, ITE, UAT, and PROD environments, ensuring operational readiness for all critical components. The PSIP team continued fixes as a result of business-side ASPP testing. In addition, they began preparation of data for the prior years to load in PROD. The investment is executing as expected.

The OS OFM Commerce Business Systems (CBS) investment continues to provide an integrated financial management system that has been implemented throughout the Department of Commerce (DOC) as well as supporting G-Invoicing activities at the bureau level.  In FY25, the investment will continue in operations and maintenance with no new planned projects. Accomplishments: Investment is supporting G-Invoicing activities at bureau level, as well as implementing mandatory updates.  Investment is meeting functional requirements. Continued with production support for G-Invoicing and Unique Entity Identifier. System availability is at 100%. Help desk response time on target. Investment is progressing as expected with low risk.

investmentName: NOAA/NESDIS/ Comprehensive Large Array-data Stewardship System (CLASS).
comment: The CLASS program continues to efficiently manage high volumes (petabytes) of satellite and in situ data and automates data ingest, quality control and access.  CLASS is the designated primary archive for most of the NOAA environmental data sets. CLASS is providing knowledge transfer to NCCF to ensure CLASS capabilities are understood. Accomplishments: Completed requirements analysis for Release 8.3.11.  Begun design of Release 8.3.11.  Metrics: Added 21.75 M new catalog files to the archive.  Operational Availability - 99.75%. The investment is executing as expected.

The Dissemination investment continues to be responsible for promoting increased accessibility, interoperability, and stewardship of NOAA data, leading, delivering, and coordinating NWS contribution to NOAA, DOC, and Administration data dissemination initiatives.  Notable Accomplishments: completed the NGITWS 3.0.0 Go Live, Spot 3.12 Go Live. There were zero Vulnerabilities found in annual DIS Cloud Penetration testing. OneNWS Network Availability: 100%. NWR Transmitter Availability: 97.85%. The investment is rated a 3 due to the risk profile and issues.

The Geographic Support Program (GSP) investment supports the integrated and automated computer-based geographic support system crucial to all censuses and household surveys. The investment continues to provide the Census address list, maps, geographic reference files, and processing systems to meet the geographic requirements of all Census Bureau programs and operations. Census counts on GSP to be able to accurately locate people and places for data collection. Accomplishments: Delivered LiMA Spatial Extract to Applications Development and Services Division(ADSD)/Listing and Mapping Application (LiMA). Delivered Boundary and Annexation Survey (BAS) 25 production pipe-delimited state-based (MAFX & MAFOP & tally files) to Enterprise Data Lake (EDL). Posted BAS pdf maps on website. Posted Partnership Shapefiles for the 2025 BAS (by state). The Investment is progressing with some risk exposure that is being mitigated.

The Central Processing investment continues to provide increased satellite network bandwidth, processing and storage capacity. It collects, communicates, processes, displays, and analyzes hydro-meteorological data that supports the NWS mission of accurate forecasts/warnings. Accomplishments: WCOSS: Continue transition of Interactive Multi-sensor Snow and Ice Mapping System (IMS) application in support of National Ice Center. NAWIPS: - AWC resolved issues found from mini-ORT of TCF desk. A full ORT will be scheduled in Spring 2025 when convective weather season starts.  PR/HFO server upgrade issue was resolved, and the product generation testing can be resumed for CPHC/TC Breakpoints desk flip.  GSL worked off the backlog and addressed operational issues from the field. AWIPS: Network Availability: 100%. Satellite Master Ground Station Availability: 100%; Met 3 out of 3 performance metrics reported. Investment is rated a 3 due to risk profile and issues.

The American Community Survey (ACS) Investment continues to support the Bureau's objective of collecting, processing, and releasing information to meet the constitutional and legislative mandates. The American Community Survey has led to a simpler decennial census, provided more timely and relevant data between censuses, and led to widespread efficiencies throughout the federal statistical system. Notable accomplishment: Completed the 5 Year Data Release DY2023 Comparison Guidance Webpage. Completed the 5 Year Table Change Webpage for 5 Year Data Release DY2023. The investment is progressing as expected.

investmentName: BIS Commerce USXPORTS Exporter Support System (CUESS)
comment: The BIS CUESS investment complements the export enforcement process in support of the single IT System for the Export Control Reform directive. BIS continues to collaborate with other agencies on the USXPORTS system for multi-agency license reviews and actively transmitting referral data. BIS continues to support the USXPORTS development for releases that improve the reliability and data efficiencies between CUESS and USXPORTS. BIS and the State Department continue to share data weekly in support of the recommendation from the GAO. Accomplishments: BIS has made significant progress in the SNAP-R hardening project. The 2030 Decennial investment covers the Design Selection Phase (FYs 2022 - 2024) for the 2030 Census.  The 2030 Census strategic goals are consistent with prior decennial census goals and include: 1) A Complete and Accurate Census, 2) Embraced and Trusted Results, 3) An Efficient and Effective Program, and 4) An Appropriately Sized, Skilled, and Structured Workforce. Operational metrics for the program is incomplete, as the structure and means to measure key performance parameters are still under development, with attainment not anticipated until closer to FOC.

The program is ?On Hold? due to funding constraints. Without funding, the program is unable to meet affordability requirements to achieve the Acquisition Decision Event 2A (ADE-2A) Milestone. Because the COP program is pre-ADE-2A, it is not yet required to deliver any of its Key Performance Parameters (KPPs), nor has reporting on operational performance metrics been established. investmentName: DHS - Federal Protective Service (FPS) Revenue Management System (RMS)
comment: Low development sprint velocity is a high risk to the program?s schedule. If the development pace remains below expectations, program may face schedule delays. The program has implemented mitigations and currently evaluating if they will effectively improve sprint velocity. RMS Release 2 was completed prior to Q4 FY24 threshold date defined in the current APB. During Q4 FY24, user satisfaction dropped slightly below operational performance target, but improved by Q1 FY25, exceeding the target.

The risk of delayed access to CISA applications related to MFA has been fully mitigated. The Okta integration has been successfully completed, and it is operational across multiple publicly facing CISA platforms to enable seamless single-sign-on functionality. This resolves earlier concerns about delayed access due to MFA. Feedback is captured ad-hoc. The program will be able to leverage surveys after ticket completion to gain feedback.

There are no high-priority risks for this program, with three low-risk items being tracked. The risk register is updated when significant changes occur, but no recent updates have been made. The program is adequately staffed with no critical vacancies. Customer feedback is collected informally during training sessions, Integrated Project Team meetings, and other interactions, and is used to guide program improvements. A formal feedback collection process is currently being developed.

A previous vendor supply chain risk has been mitigated through consistent communication with the vendor and the clear documentation of expectations in written agreements signed by all parties. Program has mitigated the risk of government information compromise by ensuring vendors adhere to security standards through regular testing and ongoing communication. Feedback is captured in an ad-hoc. Daily stand-ups with OCIO leadership are conducted to review ongoing activities and resolve any issues.

The LGDS system performance is a high risk to the program. The system does not consistently meet threshold targets for KPP or operational performance requirements. The program has taken steps to improve performance but has indicated that some requirements may be unfeasible and unnecessary. The program completed a re-baseline in Q3 FY2024, following a Q4 FY2023 breach of the ADE-3 threshold. The re-baselined APB extends the ADE-3 threshold date from Q4 FY2023 to Q4 FY2025.

The program, including initiatives such as USCG?s CGTest, is fully funded for FY25, with no gaps in the business case. A five-year funding plan is being developed to optimize resources and ensure long-term sustainability. The investment is adequately staffed with no critical vacancies. The program gathers feedback through bi-weekly stakeholder meetings to ensure that program goals align with user expectations. Status reports are provided to USCG leadership weekly.

The funding intended to support new FTEs for the AI Corps has been delayed due to the postponed enactment of the FY25 budget. The investment has identified and is correcting a funding and cost reporting error in INVEST. No critical MGMT OCIO staffing vacancies have been identified. The investment has identified and working to correct INVEST reporting errors that erroneously showed funding and cost numbers that contradicted other INVEST reporting and information provided by the investment.

The program has a funding shortfall that has led to deferring some non-essential activities and repairs. If the program does not receive requested FY25 O&S funds, the program will lack sufficient resources for maintenance and repair. The program has implemented a risk-adjusted schedule that ensures critical milestones are still being met. The core objectives of keeping the fleet operational and maintaining the most important assets have not been compromised due to the funding shortfall.

investmentName: DHS - Data Center Operations and Security
comment: Additional security controls and monitoring have been implemented to mitigate security risks associated with past EoL technology and infrastructure. A modernization project to replace EoL technologies is expected to begin in Q1 FY25 and conclude in Q1 FY26. Until the project is complete, cybersecurity risks are mitigated through the implementation of additional security controls and monitoring. Program is adequately staffed.

The UGS program was recently approved as a Level 2 Major IT/Mixed acquisition program in Q1 FY24. The program operates under significant cybersecurity risk due to its legacy status with a pending ATO deadline of Q2 FY25. The absence of a test environment creates additional vulnerability, as software updates are currently deployed directly to production without proper testing protocols. An updated LCCE accurately reflecting current scope and financial requirements will be available by Q3 FY25.

The program is adequately staffed with all of its required federal FTE positions filled. The investment?s plan to reduce the INVEST database size and resolve technical debt has been delayed due to staffing and performance issues. The INVEST infrastructure update, which was previously delayed, was completed during Q1 FY24. The investment is working to deliver Quick Reference Guides for INVEST users and a CPIC Standard Operating Procedure to improve INVEST user and CPIC administrator efficiency.

The program?s systems frequently do not meet targets for system availability, reliability, and maintainability due to DEC outages and failures. Since an FY22 cut, the investment?s annual appropriated budget has been short of its cost requirement. The shortfall has been covered with funds from the COP program and funding from the HIFLD program before it was transitioned to the investment in FY23. In FY25, the investment will deploy the recently developed and tested enterprise management system.

TraCSS will ingest, archive, process, and disseminate Space Situational Awareness (SSA) data and products for space safety and sustainability and will provide conjunction analysis and warning services to commercial satellite owner/operators. Accomplishments: TraCSS Phase 1.0 went live on 9/30/2024, entering beta test period to evaluate and enhance commercial satellite operators' experience with NOAA-produced conjunction analysis products. investmentName: Census - Data Ingest and Collection for the Enterprise (DICE)
comment: The Data Ingest and Collection for the Enterprise (DICE) investment continues with implementing a new way of doing business that focuses on minimizing redundancy, lowering complexity, and avoiding duplicative costs for the Census's business and household data ingest and collection operations. DICE continues the efforts of being able to provide a way to collect quality data using one source. This will cause a significant risk to the program?s FOC schedule and delay several FY24 priorities. Due to the PC&I funding shortfall, executing development contract options in Q4 FY24 depends on reallocating O&M funds to PC&I, which will prevent development delays and staff loss.

The program is adequately staffed with no reported critical vacancies. The program does not currently measure stakeholders? feedback but receives verbal feedback on a regular basis for the strategic plan implementation, which resulted in the stakeholder providing very satisfactory feedback. The program reports no open GAO or OIG audits. The investment tracks risks in the INVEST tool. The program reviews and updates risks on a monthly basis.

The program has resolved its major risks by hiring a director and additional key personnel. The risk register is reviewed monthly with the A&LS Risk Management Plan. A&LS communicates feedback with XDD to identify any technical changes that may need to be made in the LMS training environment. The program reports that it has improved public-facing website scanning score, reflecting enhanced accessibility measures.

The ECC virtualization project, which was intended to mitigate the risks of aging infrastructure, has been cancelled. This
follows the cancellation of the ECC cloud migration project in FY2023. A plan to refresh hardware is under development. As a result of project delays and cancellations, the ECC system continues to depend on secondary/backup hardware that is past EoS. The program?s risk/issue probability and impact are not defined, nor are risk triggers or closure criteria.

The program is adequately staffed. All risks listed are categorized as low or medium risk impact to the program. There are still two open OIG audits that remain overdue that continue to be addressed. The program reports daily engagement with program offices to ensure cybersecurity/compliance requirements are communicated and met. Due to an ongoing protest, the program reports that it will miss the Q4 FY2024 Zero-Trust implementation target.

The target date to transition all circuits has been delayed from Q3 FY24 to Q4 FY25 due to a lack of bids from vendors, circuit delays, high cost of circuit buildout in some locations, site leasing delays, and other logistical challenges. The threshold target for one KPI was not achieved in FY23 and is not on target for FY24. Due to insufficient O&M funding, constrained federal staffing resources, and new requirements, the program is only able to address the highest-priority user requirements.

investmentName: DHS - CIO - Identity Credential and Access Management (ICAM)
comment: The program faces an unexpected financial deficit due to the withdrawal of DHS Components. The program has 2 critical vacancies and needs additional staff to support workload distribution and prevent burnout among the existing team. The migration of customers to the DHSAuthPortal system will be completed by Q4 FY2024. ICAM is actively managing expectations with the remaining applications, and a final analysis will be performed post-deadline to ensure all applications are migrated.

The program reports the overall deployment timeline will be delayed, and operational efficiency will decrease if the deployment of kiosks is hindered by supply chain concerns, specifically the lack of TAA compliant hardware. An updated risk register was provided that includes risk descriptions, and impact scores but does not include mitigation strategies. The investment continues to meet customer expectations as indicated through monthly customer service reports and engagements with components.

The program faces significant risk in not securing replacement PC&I funding in its FY25 budget. The absence of FY25 funding has resulted in a schedule variance. The unavailability of additional funding is impeding the program's progress in completing the modernization of tools and systems. The program is coordinating with the ISD leadership and budget team to resolve the funding issue. CISA Gateway is exceeding all operational targets with performance metrics meeting established thresholds.

The program met/exceeded threshold values for all operational performance metrics this assessment period. The sufficiency rate is identified in the OA as a key priority that the program continues to exceed. The APIS database migration has been delayed from Q4 FY24 to Q2 FY25 because the intended migration solution could not be used, given the scale of the inflow and outflow of data and message queries. The program successfully executed its mitigation plan and identified an alternate solution.

The TWIC program is meeting all key performance metrics. The program has no critical vacancies. The transition from the TWIC v7 to v8 credentials, known as the NEXGEN transition, has been successfully completed as of Q4 FY24. agencyName: Department of Housing and Urban Development
comment: The Single Family Housing investment has one project, Federal Housing Administration Modernization FHA Catalyst.  The FHA Catalyst initiative began as a multi-year investment to modernize FHA's IT systems.  The program supports IT development projects that modernize the FHA Loan Lifecyle as authorized by HUD's Housing IT modernization.  This project is at a Moderately High-Risk level.  When reviewing the WBS, there are major milestones and activities that are significantly delayed.  For example, the development of FHA Catalyst modules  was to be completed by May of 2024, but this has not yet been completed.  Activities involving Program Management and Program Support with similar projected completion dates of May 2024 also have not yet been completed.  Additionally, there are activities listed in the WBS that do not provide a projected start/end date, which should be reported.  Because of the WBS variances and delays noted from the FHA Catalyst project, this investment is scored a 2.

agencyName: Department of Housing and Urban Development
comment: Since the last CIO Rating submission in January of 2024, HUD started work in June and has made progress to automate the CPD Grant Closeout Project. This project provides necessary enhancements that reduce administrative burdens to both HUD staff and grantees by reducing manual/paper processes. In addition to the CPD Grant Closeout Project, the Department started work in April on the eSNAPS project to replace, modernize and stabilize the information systems automating HUD's Continuum of Care program for homeless assistance. While progress has been made towards the Investment, there are variances reported in Folio with the Economic Development Initiative (EDI). The project currently reports a 50% cost variance ($4 million planned vs $2 million projected) and a 48% schedule variance.  The project was originally planned to be completed by October 2024, but the Department is now anticipating completion by June 2025. These variance percentages would classify the EDI project as High Risk. Of the three active projects reported in FOLIO within the Enterprise Management Investment, eSNAPS and Automate CPD Grant Closeout Project are in good project health and pose low risk. However, because the EDI project poses a High Risk level, this investment is at a 3 or Medium Risk level.

agencyName: Department of Housing and Urban Development
comment: The Financial Management Technology Support Investment provides support for HUD enterprise financial management systems, including interface with shared service core financial system. HUD continues to address the overall financial requirements and to improve the reliability, quality, and availability of financial data. The Department is beginning to modernize the disbursement and funds control system used for many grants and subsidy programs. Congress recently approved a Performance Plan for a multi-year initiative to establish a new interface with the core financial system bypassing the legacy mainframe system. In FY 2024, there are no projects reported in Folio for this IT Investment. This IT Investment scored a 4 or Moderately Low Risk level.

agencyName: Department of Housing and Urban Development
comment: The Multifamily and Health Care Facilities Investment has two projects listed in FOLIO. First, the TRACS project is focused on system modifications for HOTMA that will change how deductions from income are calculated and allow for periodic Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA) Changes. Planned completion date for this project was July 31, 2024, but the project has experienced delays related to activities around Sprint 4 and 5 of the projects. These delays push projected completion date to the end of November 2024, which is a 23% schedule variance. The second project under the Multifamily and Health Care Facilities Investment is AUSS/PLUS. AUSS/PLUS focuses on the continued development of proof-of-concept AUSS into production ready PLUS, the replacement of legacy DAP system and other MF capabilities for underwriting and closing of FHA-insured mortgages. Based on the data reported in Folio, there are a few concerns that factored into the rating for this investment. When looking at the project’s Work Breakdown Structure (WBS), there are three activities behind schedule relating to functional release, user ready release, and lender portal releases. Two of these activities do not provide a projected end date, which should be reported in FOLIO. Additionally, the project uses an iterative monthly Agile process, but the WBS activities do not reflect or show this. Lastly, the total actual costs reported in Folio is $1,832 but this was reported in error. Based on the data provided in FOLIO and the concerns previously mentioned, the AUSS/PLUS project poses a Moderately High Risk level. Because of the schedule variances for both TRACS and AUSS/PLUS, combined with the other concerns noted above, this IT Investment is scored at a 2 or Moderately High Risk.

agencyName: Department of Housing and Urban Development
comment: In FY 2024, there are seven active projects under the Public and Assisted Housing Oversight Investment. They are the PIH Housing Information Portal, NSPIRE, Native Advantage, Modernization of Public Housing Portal, Mod of PIH Data Warehouse, Grants Enterprise Management System (GEMS), and Energy and Performance Information Center. All seven of these projects report a cost variance and/or schedule variance. The PIH Housing Information Portal, NSPIRE, and Mod of PIH Data Warehouse projects are at a High Risk level. While the PIH Housing Information Portal does not report any cost variances, the Department now anticipates it to be delayed almost 2 years, or a 60% schedule variance. The original completion date was planned for October of 2023 and the new projected completion date is August of 2025. In looking at the WBS, there are delays in activities around PHA scoring methodology, Core Portal, Capital Fund, and 2024 HOTMA Compliance. With regards to the NSPIRE project, HUD reports a 35% schedule variance. This project had a planned implementation and completion by August 2024, but completion is now anticipated by August 2025. According to the project’s WBS, delays are related to system integrations and multi-family implementation activities. The remaining projects within this Investment are either medium or low risk. The Native Advantage project reports both medium risks to cost and schedule. Projected completion of the Native Advantage project is delayed five months from end of August 2024 to February 2025. Additionally, HUD anticipates this project to cost more than planned from $4.8 million to $5.4 million. The overages and delays place the project at 14% cost variance and 12% schedule variance. When considering all seven of the Public and Assisted Housing Oversight’s projects in FY 2024, this Investment should be scored at a Moderately High Risk level or a 2.

investmentName: BIS Commerce USXPORTS Exporter Support System (CUESS)
comment: The BIS CUESS investment complements the export enforcement process in support of the single IT System for the Export Control Reform directive. BIS continues to collaborate with other agencies on the USXPORTS system for multi-agency license reviews and actively transmitting referral data. BIS continues to support the USXPORTS development for releases that improve the reliability and data efficiencies between CUESS and USXPORTS. BIS and the State Department continue to share data weekly in support of the recommendation from the GAO. Accomplishments: Completed internal testing of core SNAP-R features, created design documents for Self-Management features, and started Self-Management component implementation. Snowflake and Report Migration: Performed usability testing on AES Analysis Reports with EMCD and MCD users to verify the usability of the dashboard. User Research: Conducted leadership interviews on the current business processes for reviewing license applications. Conducted onsite business process mapping workshops with license officers to collect details on current process for the License Application Process’s Service Blueprint, baselining that for future process mapping.  Investment is progressing with risks.

investmentName: OS OFM Commerce Business Applications Solution (BAS) V2
comment: The BAS program is a DOC IT modernization effort to deploy an integrated suite of financial and business management applications in support of our mission using a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS), cloud-computing environment. The BAS program continues to modernize the Department's financial management, acquisition, and property systems.  The Secretary and Deputy Secretary of Commerce have made the decision to postpone the NIST deployment until October 2026.  Census will deploy October 2025 as originally scheduled. Notable Accomplishments: Continued planning sessions conducted to adjust project schedules and timelines to reflect delay in deployment of system for NOAA, BIS, and EDA. The program rating is based on replanning, risks, and continuing to work through organizational change management risks and challenges to user adoption.

Enterprise Product Line continues to manage all of the back-office operations including communicating with the public and employees, providing usable data collections and analytics, disseminating public records including assignment records, collecting fees, paying agency bills, supporting legal functions, providing HR capabilities, supporting budget and planning, and managing facilities and assets. Accomplishments: Completed the implementation of the PTOWeb Search Entry Point into Drupal, providing users with additional search capabilities to quickly find information. CC&A: Completed the integration of OpenID Connect (OIDC) to enhance authentication and identity management for internal user of CCC, which improves security and simplifies the login experience. Realized a 6.98% in technical debt reduction for the FY2024. Incremental production deployments trending at 150 minimum per FY quarter. Investment is progressing with risks and issues that are being mitigated

The OS OFM Commerce Business Systems (CBS) investment continues to provide an integrated financial management system that has been implemented throughout the Department of Commerce (DOC) as well as supporting G-Invoicing activities at the bureau level.  In FY24, the investment will continue in operations and maintenance with no new planned projects. Accomplishments: Investment is supporting G-Invoicing activities at bureau level, as well as implementing mandatory updates.  Investment is meeting functional requirements. Unique Entity Identifier:  Continued with production support. System availability is at 100%. Help desk response time on target. Investment is progressing as expected with low risk.

The Patents Product Line investment continues to support the Patents business by creating additional products, retiring/decommissioning more legacy systems; and supporting Patents products operational activities. Notable Accomplishments: Deployed a new service to flatten a PDF file to improve conversion success rate thus reducing document loading delays and improving resiliency. Completed Oracle 19c license reduction for Real Application Cluster database servers to ensure cost savings and licensing compliance. Improvements in search system performance by way of managing impactful search queries to increase resiliency.  Investment is progressing with risks and issues that are being mitigated.

investmentName: NOAA/OCIO/ NOAA R&D High Performance Computing System (HPCS)
comment: HPCS continues to be a constellation of super computers used by NOAA to perform research and development to improve climate and weather models that is meeting the mission requirements in performance.  The HPCS investment is in Operational and Maintenance mode and consistently meets and exceeds performance metrics. Accomplishments: System availability 99.12%; Data availability 100%; Compute hours made available 540,481,536. R&D HPCS Program rated as Yellow due to funding deficiency and capacity shortfall - $20M reduction in FY2024 will have O&M impacts for FY 2025, 256PF is the ultimate goal to meet 100% requirement.  Progressing with some risk and issues on capacity impacting the rating.

investmentName: NOAA/OSC/Civilian Traffic Coordination System for Space (TraCSS)
comment: TraCSS is the Department of Commerce's enterprise solution civil space traffic coordination investment to meet Space Policy Directive 3 issued in 2018.  Directive 3 designates the Department of Commerce as the lead civilian agency for providing basic SSA data and STM services to commercial space operators.  On behalf of DOC, NOAA's Office of Space Commerce is developing the Traffic Coordination System for Space TraCSS. TraCSS will ingest, archive, process, and disseminate Space Situational Awareness (SSA) data and products for space safety and sustainability and will provide conjunction analysis and warning services to commercial satellite owner/operators. Accomplishments: The initial phase of NOAA’s Traffic Coordination System for Space (TraCSS) has begun delivering spaceflight safety services to a beta group of satellite operators. Today, for the first time, satellite operators are receiving basic space situational awareness (SSA) data and space traffic coordination (STC) services. The investment is progressing with some risk that is being mitigated.

The Trademark Product Line investment continues to maintain all Trademark legacy components across the product line and is in the process of developing modernized business and technical solutions to further improve the delivery of business value. Notable Accomplishments: Successfully deployed eFile Phase 1 Release 10 open beta, enhancements, and defect fixes to the production environment. Successfully deployed TTABIS priority enhancements and defect fixes to the production environment. Successfully deployed TM Exam related enhancements [Office Actions] and defect fixes to production environment. Successfully deployed Unassigned docket Web UI upgrades as part of the modernization of the Legacy MCRP application. Investment is progressing with some risks that are being mitigated.

investmentName: Census - Data Ingest and Collection for the Enterprise (DICE)
comment: The Data Ingest and Collection for the Enterprise (DICE) investment continues with implementing a new way of doing business that focuses on minimizing redundancy, lowering complexity, and avoiding duplicative costs for the Census's business and household data ingest and collection operations. DICE continues the efforts of being able to provide a way to collect quality data using one source. The program also continues its efforts to integrate and manage the development of an enterprise system that provides a shared platform for receiving data that has been collected by external sources, census, and survey data. Accomplishments: DICE is making significant strides in its AIES-23 production, currently reaching a 60.5% completion rate. DICE has been actively engaged in testing various CPS-ISR. These field tests are crucial for validating the performance and reliability of the systems under real-world conditions. Investment is improving in reporting and is progressing in execution but is operating with risk exposure.

The Geographic Support Program (GSP) investment supports the integrated and automated computer-based geographic support system crucial to all censuses and household surveys. The investment continues to provide the Census address list, maps, geographic reference files, and processing systems to meet the geographic requirements of all Census Bureau programs and operations. Census counts on GSP to be able to accurately locate people and places for data collection. Accomplishments: This month GSP continues to provide updates to Census address list, maps, geographic reference file such as SAS Master Address file along with Address Extract Data dump files to conduct the most accurate surveys and censuses. Delivering Merged Geodatabases for the Social, Economic, and Housing Statistics Division (SEHSD) School Districts via Kiteworks represents a significant advancement in data accessibility and collaboration. This process ensures that comprehensive geospatial data is seamlessly integrated, providing essential insights into school district demographics, economic conditions, and housing statistics. The Investment is progressing with some risk exposure that is being mitigated.

The 2030 Decennial investment covers the Design Selection Phase (FYs 2022 - 2024) for the 2030 Census.  The 2030 Census strategic goals are consistent with prior decennial census goals and include: 1) A Complete and Accurate Census, 2) Embraced and Trusted Results, 3) An Efficient and Effective Program, and 4) An Appropriately Sized, Skilled, and Structured Workforce. This investment is currently in the Design Selection Phase for the 2030 Census and on target to meet all scheduled milestones. Accomplishments:  The 2030 Census delivered multiple Research Results Reports to DPMO Document Management Team.  These reports describe the activities for managing the work required to meet the 2030 Census Program’s mission, vision, and goals, as documented in the 2030 Census Strategy. The 2030 Census developed the IT Solutions Requirements Management Plan. This document provides the IT solution providers with the details they need to produce the solution in manageable, time-bound chunks. The investment is progressing as expected.

Enterprise Data Lake continues to be a flexible data repository intended to provide the Census Bureau with a next generation scaling capability to fulfill data storage, reporting, analytics, and security needs while reducing costs associated with duplicative data silos. Notable Accomplishments: Automated CloudWatch alert creation for provisioned services (EC2, RDS, Redshift, and Aurora). Extended S3 Mounts and Grants to users working in the new Multi-account environments. Completed enhancements to the Instance Scheduler for more efficient coordination with the RHEL Patching schedule. IRE Migration: CODS successfully tested Lakehouse Multi-account S3 access automation. The investment is rated 3 due to risk exposure and reporting concerns.

The American Community Survey (ACS) Investment continues to support the Bureau's objective of collecting, processing, and releasing information to meet the constitutional and legislative mandates. The American Community Survey has led to a simpler decennial census, provided more timely and relevant data between censuses, and led to widespread efficiencies throughout the federal statistical system. Notable accomplishment:  Completed the 1-Year Summary File Documentation Webpage for the 1-Year Data Release DY2023. Completed the 1-Year Tables Changes Webpage for the 1-Year Data Release DY2023.  The investment is progressing as expected.

investmentName: BEA Estimation Information Technology System (BEA-EITS) for Measuring the Changing US Economy.
comment: The BEA Estimation IT System encompasses BEA's core economic processing system, and directly supports BEA's mission.  This investment continues to support timely, accurate release of more than 60 critical economic estimates per year. The BEA-EITS for Measuring the Changing U.S. Economy continues to support production and dissemination of BEA's critical economic estimates as well as statistical confidentiality, including legal requirements. BEA is pursuing a Statistical Production Modernization program which seeks to simplify and modernize processes and tools by first completing business process reengineering and then updating. Accomplishments: Supported the timely, relevant, and accurate release of the following data sets (U.S. International Transactions, 2nd Quarter 2024, U.S. International Investment Position, 2nd Quarter 2024, Gross Domestic Product, 2nd Quarter 2024 (Third Estimate), GDP by Industry, and Corporate Profits (Revised), Personal Income and Outlays, August 2024, Gross Domestic Product by State and Personal Income by State, 2nd Quarter 2024). In FY2025 this investment is being remapped into four (4) new investments, 2 majora BEA-Collection and Dissemination, BEA-Statistical Applications, one non-major BEA-Research and one standard BEA-Business Support Applications.

The Central Processing investment continues to provide increased satellite network bandwidth, processing and storage capacity. It collects, communicates, processes, displays, and analyzes hydro-meteorological data that supports the NWS mission of accurate forecasts/warnings. Accomplishments: WCOSS: Continue transition of Interactive Multi-sensor Snow and Ice Mapping System (IMS) application in support of National Ice Center. NAWIPS: AWC ORT complete for Convective-SIGMET and Tropical desk.  AWC pre-ORT testing of whiteboard localapp complete for TCF desk, which is required for scheduling ORT.  NHC has started to issue watches/warning and graphical products using AWIPS in the 2024 hurricane season. Hazard Services: ABQ and MTR issued operational hazards from v4 ATAN.  Met with fire weather SMEs to finalize requirements. AWIPS: Customer Results and Network Availability: 100%. Network restoration in under 4 min. Satellite Master Ground Station Availability: 100%; Met 5 out of 5 performance metrics reported. Investment is rated a 3 due to risk profile and issues.

The Dissemination investment continues to be responsible for promoting increased accessibility, interoperability, and stewardship of NOAA data, leading, delivering, and coordinating NWS contribution to NOAA, DOC, and Administration data dissemination initiatives.  Notable Accomplishments - ISatSS 5.2 Go Live. NWWS-OI Onboarding on IDP. Weather.gov/Ingest Onboarding on IDP. 30 Percent expansion of Flood Inundation Maps (FIM) Released. The investment is rated a 3 due to the risk profile and issues.

investmentName: NOAA/NESDIS/ Comprehensive Large Array-data Stewardship System (CLASS).
comment: The CLASS program continues to efficiently manage high volumes (petabytes) of satellite and in situ data and automates data ingest, quality control and access.  CLASS is the designated primary archive for most of the NOAA environmental data sets. CLASS is providing knowledge transfer to NCCF to ensure CLASS capabilities are understood. Accomplishments:  Completed design for Release 8.3.10. Conducted tabletop exercise for Business Continuity Plan (BCP) annual test and submit report. Performance metrics: Added 20.23 M new catalog files to the archive.  Operational Availability - 99.39%. The investment is executing as expected.

The Economic Censuses and Surveys program is a mixed life cycle investment and continues to support statistical programs that count and profile U.S. businesses and government organizations. ECON investment accomplishments include: The DIPSE Redesign Team implemented bug fixes for Coverage Change Request Search, Enterprise NAICS Display, Company Status, and other modules. The AIES/SPACE team successfully provisioned Aurora databases across DEV, ITE, UAT, and PROD environments, ensuring operational readiness for all critical components. The PSIP team completed gathering requirements and documenting the process flow for ASPP. They started design and development for the ASPP Methodology module based on the final requirements. The investment is executing as expected.

investmentName: Census - Center for Enterprise Dissemination Services and Consumer Information (CEDSCI).
comment: The Program and the CEDSCI EDDE IT Platform project continues to be dedicated to using customer feedback to develop innovative ways to improve customer with improved data and product displays, searches, and downloads accessible from census.gov and on mobile devices. The project is in the development of a modernized platform that disseminates Census data in an efficient technological manner.  The program is responsible for both the development project plus using the new platform for disseminating Census data.  Notable Accomplishments: In FY24 Q4, CEDSCI reorganized codeset and geography filters to aid in data discoverability. The program added helper text for ACS 1-Year tables and maps, integrated search by address into the main search, and added support for more geography types. CEDSCI completed the 2020 Census Detailed and Supplemental Demographic and Housing Characteristics Files.  In addition, the investment completed Sprint 16 and Sprint 17 in FY2024.  The investment continues to have a risk exposure contributing to the overall rating.
