agencyName: Department of Housing and Urban Development
comment: Since the last CIO Rating submission in January of 2024, HUD started work in June and has made progress to automate the CPD Grant Closeout Project. This project provides necessary enhancements that reduce administrative burdens to both HUD staff and grantees by reducing manual/paper processes. In addition to the CPD Grant Closeout Project, the Department started work in April on the eSNAPS project to replace, modernize and stabilize the information systems automating HUD's Continuum of Care program for homeless assistance. While progress has been made towards the Investment, there are variances reported in Folio with the Economic Development Initiative (EDI). The project currently reports a 50% cost variance ($4 million planned vs $2 million projected) and a 48% schedule variance.  The project was originally planned to be completed by October 2024, but the Department is now anticipating completion by June 2025. These variance percentages would classify the EDI project as High Risk. Of the three active projects reported in FOLIO within the Enterprise Management Investment, eSNAPS and Automate CPD Grant Closeout Project are in good project health and pose low risk. However, because the EDI project poses a High Risk level, this investment is at a 3 or Medium Risk level.

agencyName: Department of Housing and Urban Development
comment: The Multifamily and Health Care Facilities Investment has two projects listed in FOLIO. First, the TRACS project is focused on system modifications for HOTMA that will change how deductions from income are calculated and allow for periodic Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA) Changes. Planned completion date for this project was July 31, 2024, but the project has experienced delays related to activities around Sprint 4 and 5 of the projects. These delays push projected completion date to the end of November 2024, which is a 23% schedule variance. The second project under the Multifamily and Health Care Facilities Investment is AUSS/PLUS. AUSS/PLUS focuses on the continued development of proof-of-concept AUSS into production ready PLUS, the replacement of legacy DAP system and other MF capabilities for underwriting and closing of FHA-insured mortgages. Based on the data reported in Folio, there are a few concerns that factored into the rating for this investment. When looking at the project’s Work Breakdown Structure (WBS), there are three activities behind schedule relating to functional release, user ready release, and lender portal releases. Two of these activities do not provide a projected end date, which should be reported in FOLIO. Additionally, the project uses an iterative monthly Agile process, but the WBS activities do not reflect or show this. Lastly, the total actual costs reported in Folio is $1,832 but this was reported in error. Based on the data provided in FOLIO and the concerns previously mentioned, the AUSS/PLUS project poses a Moderately High Risk level. Because of the schedule variances for both TRACS and AUSS/PLUS, combined with the other concerns noted above, this IT Investment is scored at a 2 or Moderately High Risk.

agencyName: Department of Housing and Urban Development
comment: The Single Family Housing investment has one project, Federal Housing Administration Modernization FHA Catalyst.  The FHA Catalyst initiative began as a multi-year investment to modernize FHA's IT systems.  The program supports IT development projects that modernize the FHA Loan Lifecyle as authorized by HUD's Housing IT modernization.  This project is at a Moderately High-Risk level.  When reviewing the WBS, there are major milestones and activities that are significantly delayed.  For example, the development of FHA Catalyst modules  was to be completed by May of 2024, but this has not yet been completed.  Activities involving Program Management and Program Support with similar projected completion dates of May 2024 also have not yet been completed.  Additionally, there are activities listed in the WBS that do not provide a projected start/end date, which should be reported.  Because of the WBS variances and delays noted from the FHA Catalyst project, this investment is scored a 2.

agencyName: Department of Housing and Urban Development
comment: In FY 2024, there are seven active projects under the Public and Assisted Housing Oversight Investment. They are the PIH Housing Information Portal, NSPIRE, Native Advantage, Modernization of Public Housing Portal, Mod of PIH Data Warehouse, Grants Enterprise Management System (GEMS), and Energy and Performance Information Center. All seven of these projects report a cost variance and/or schedule variance. The PIH Housing Information Portal, NSPIRE, and Mod of PIH Data Warehouse projects are at a High Risk level. While the PIH Housing Information Portal does not report any cost variances, the Department now anticipates it to be delayed almost 2 years, or a 60% schedule variance. The original completion date was planned for October of 2023 and the new projected completion date is August of 2025. In looking at the WBS, there are delays in activities around PHA scoring methodology, Core Portal, Capital Fund, and 2024 HOTMA Compliance. With regards to the NSPIRE project, HUD reports a 35% schedule variance. This project had a planned implementation and completion by August 2024, but completion is now anticipated by August 2025. According to the project’s WBS, delays are related to system integrations and multi-family implementation activities. The remaining projects within this Investment are either medium or low risk. The Native Advantage project reports both medium risks to cost and schedule. Projected completion of the Native Advantage project is delayed five months from end of August 2024 to February 2025. Additionally, HUD anticipates this project to cost more than planned from $4.8 million to $5.4 million. The overages and delays place the project at 14% cost variance and 12% schedule variance. When considering all seven of the Public and Assisted Housing Oversight’s projects in FY 2024, this Investment should be scored at a Moderately High Risk level or a 2.

RISKS: USAID is proactively addressing cybersecurity and privacy risks to safeguard its mission and infrastructure. As the agency empowers its staff with development authorizations, the dependency on secure systems and applications intensifies, presenting significant challenges. Recent geopolitical events, such as the Russia-Ukraine conflict and tensions in the Southern Levant, have exposed vulnerabilities in detecting and countering Advanced Persistent Threats and Nation State Actors, leading to increased risks of disruption and espionage. Emerging threats targeting mobile applications, supply chains, and the surveillance of high-level officials have also been identified. MITIGATION: To counter these risks, USAID is investing in a robust team of cybersecurity and procurement experts, as well as cutting-edge technologies, all within the framework of federal laws, regulations, and policies. The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) enhances security measures, reducing the time needed to detect and respond to threats. This strategic approach enables USAID to: a) Deploy automated and often preemptive measures against new threats, regulatory changes, and technological advancements. b) Enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of the Cybersecurity Framework and privacy controls, which are essential for maintaining cyber hygiene and risk management. These measures are subject to audits by oversight bodies such as the Office of Inspector General (OIG), the Government Accountability Office (GAO), and others. Through these mitigation strategies, USAID aims to fortify its defenses against cyber threats and ensure the integrity of its operations and the privacy of sensitive information.

This quarter the Data Center Assessment remains a moderately low risk.  All investments consider cloud first and we continue virtualization of the on-premise storage.  Our multi-cloud contract (AWS, Azure and Google) continues to provide new opportunities for artificial intelligence (AI), application development, testing and migrations to the cloud.  Additionally we are close to completing our data center modernization project which will improve redundancy and resiliency, in addition to implementing a new network monitoring tool.

This quarter the End User standard investment rating has remains low risk.  The customer service metrics continue to exceed thresholds.  We continue to improve our baselines and hardware asset management.  We continue our collaboration with the Department of Justice on several tools for ZTA which also improve our End User support.

NARA is still working towards implementing PIV/MFA authentication for its systems and applications.  Currently PIV and optional MFA for public identities is enabled for 43% of NARA major FISMA systems.  Work is underway to add an additional 13 systems this year.  NARA is continuing to make further progress towards its ZTA capabilities, and has established initial operating capabilities for making its major systems over the internet through a combination of services provided through the Department of Justice and their Justice Edge Trusted Services (JETS) and through Microsoft Conditional Access.  NARA will continue to implement these solutions for additional systems and users within NARA.  NARA also has ongoing work to establish and expand its identity management solution capability through Microsoft Entra ID.

This quarter the Network standard investment risk remains relatively low. We have several key projects on-going to upgrade and replace aging technology including our wireless infrastructure, network switches and the transition to Voice over IP (VoIP).  All of these projects will improve performance and minimize risk of hardware failure.  Additionally we are implementing redundant circuits at our critical sites.  We have increased contract resources to assist with the design and implementation of key initiatives such as Infrastructure upgrades, IPv6 and Enterprise Wi-Fi.

The NARA 801 CPIC Directive should be promulgated soon.  Three charters were reviewed and updated this quarter.  CPICs operations guide and other documentation is being updated on a continuous basis.  NARA 805 SDLC is being updated to reflect current practices and clearly identify Agile processes.  The agency continues to support required staffing across the organization as well.

NextGen HMS Go-Live was achieved with a four-phased rollout of the modernized system, however, multiple features and system workarounds remain in the product backlog that will require additional development to improve on the initial release. ENOS modernization is not funded for FY25 and may require internal development to avoid the risk of operating the legacy system on the Siebel platform with the O&M contract ending 09/25. NextGen DAS is behind schedule. New development uses an agile and continuous development approach while maintaining product backlogs that track stakeholders needs. Project and system performance is tracked and measured to ensure metrics are on target.

NextGen ARCIS and CMRS projects improved but their are still schedule delays.  NextGen CMRS UAT phase began 05/20/24 and was extended at the request of the product owner team.  Additional development required for MVP identified during UAT.  Working with the Contracting Office to extend the timeline to perform additional development, UAT and conduct training with new estimated timeline in January 2025.  NextGen ARCIS has completed seven of 22 planned sprints.  Two additional sprints added to recover from lower than projected velocity in first three sprints.  Development planned for completion in May 2025 with rollout in late July.  The ERA 2.0 Program has dealt with some challenges in vendor performance over the last few months, but through some proactive measures with our Contracting Officer and his representatives we have forced some key vendor changes and are working with new leadership to address the critical infrastructure upgrades facing the program over the next year.

investmentName: NOAA/OSC/Civilian Traffic Coordination System for Space (TraCSS)
comment: TraCSS is the Department of Commerce's enterprise solution civil space traffic coordination investment to meet Space Policy Directive 3 issued in 2018.  Directive 3 designates the Department of Commerce as the lead civilian agency for providing basic SSA data and STM services to commercial space operators.  On behalf of DOC, NOAA's Office of Space Commerce is developing the Traffic Coordination System for Space TraCSS. TraCSS will ingest, archive, process, and disseminate Space Situational Awareness (SSA) data and products for space safety and sustainability and will provide conjunction analysis and warning services to commercial satellite owner/operators. Accomplishments Government product owners engaged throughout sprint cycle. Government PMO engaged in biweekly demos and product backlog grooming. PMO alternates sending personnel in-person for demos. Parsons (SI) participated in DoD workshop for synchronization. The investment is progressing towards an IOC of September 2024.

New AWS Services - AWS Aurora planning migrations of Postgres RDS. IRE Data Transfer - Continued progress with FSx access automation and bidirectional sync. Completed ACLs with initial data migration. Refactored access automation to work with new AWS accounts. The investment is rated 3 due to risk exposure and reporting concerns.

The Geographic Support Program (GSP) investment supports the integrated and automated computer-based geographic support system crucial to all censuses and household surveys. The investment continues to provide the Census address list, maps, geographic reference files, and processing systems to meet the geographic requirements of all Census Bureau programs and operations. Census counts on GSP to be able to accurately locate people and places for data collection. Accomplishments: GSP continues to provide master address test files along with Test SAS Geographic Reference files. This month GSP continues to provide updates to Census address list, maps, geographic reference file to conduct the most accurate surveys and censuses. Investment is progressing with some risk exposure that is being mitigated.

The American Community Survey (ACS) Investment continues to support the Bureau's objective of collecting, processing, and releasing information to meet the constitutional and legislative mandates. The American Community Survey has led to a simpler decennial census, provided more timely and relevant data between censuses, and led to widespread efficiencies throughout the federal statistical system. Notable accomplishment:  Closed out the Frame Creation for Data Year 2023. Completed the 1-Year Auto Review Tool (ART) for the 1-Year Data Review Data Year 2023. Completed the 2024 Group Quarters Systems Test.  The investment is progressing as expected.

The 2030 Decennial investment covers the Design Selection Phase (FYs 2022 - 2024) for the 2030 Census.  The 2030 Census strategic goals are consistent with prior decennial census goals and include: 1) A Complete and Accurate Census, 2) Embraced and Trusted Results, 3) An Efficient and Effective Program, and 4) An Appropriately Sized, Skilled, and Structured Workforce. The three major areas of work in addition to general planning activities are work related to:  Design Selection, EA Research, and The 2026 Census Test. The investment is progressing as expected.

investmentName: BEA Estimation Information Technology System (BEA-EITS) for Measuring the Changing US Economy.
comment: The BEA Estimation IT System encompasses BEA's core economic processing system, and directly supports BEA's mission.  This investment continues to support timely, accurate release of more than 60 critical economic estimates per year. The BEA-EITS for Measuring the Changing U.S. Economy continues to support production and dissemination of BEA's critical economic estimates as well as statistical confidentiality, including legal requirements. BEA is pursuing a Statistical Production Modernization program which seeks to simplify and modernize processes and tools by first completing business process reengineering and then updating. Accomplishments: Supported the timely, relevant, and accurate release of the U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services, March 2024 data sets. End User (OCS): Pilot WebEx E2EE meeting to identify and resolve issues prior to GDP lockup. Completed Single Device setup for National Economic Directorate. Supported Treasury Enterprise TIC relocation cutover, to include verifying routing and connectivity from BEA to https://hrconnect.treasury.gov. This investment is progressing with some risk that are being addressed.

investmentName: NOAA/OSC/Civilian Traffic Coordination System for Space (TraCSS)
comment: TraCSS is the Department of Commerce's enterprise solution civil space traffic coordination investment to meet Space Policy Directive 3 issued in 2018.  Directive 3 designates the Department of Commerce as the lead civilian agency for providing basic SSA data and STM services to commercial space operators.  On behalf of DOC, NOAA's Office of Space Commerce is developing the Traffic Coordination System for Space TraCSS. TraCSS will ingest, archive, process, and disseminate Space Situational Awareness (SSA) data and products for space safety and sustainability and will provide conjunction analysis and warning services to commercial satellite owner/operators. Accomplishments: PM selected, pending screening process. Continued sprint planning with Parsons (Systems Integrator). Consolidated pathfinder operational and extended by 1 month.  A TraCSS Listening Session: Space Data Standards and Formats-Orbit Comprehensive Message was held. The Office of Space Commerce released a Vision for Global SSA Coordination. The investment is progressing towards an IOC of September 2024.

Enterprise Product Line continues to manage all of the back-office operations including communicating with the public and employees, providing usable data collections and analytics, disseminating public records including assignment records, collecting fees, paying agency bills, supporting legal functions, providing HR capabilities, supporting budget and planning, and managing facilities and assets. Accomplishments: For our 3rd Quarter to date, the investment accepted 56% of planned deliveries with 44% remaining activity in the workflow for this release; 87% of the annual budget is executed with 12.6% remaining and on target for execution before end of FY. Delivered the Enterprise Telework Information System (ETIS) Recertification enhancements, to enable users to view and recertify their telework agreements online in compliance with the Business Unit and Agency recertification requirements. Legal Tools:  Progressed 82% with Office of Enrollment and Discipline Information System (OEDIS) Enhancements to include but not limited to reducing the number of times a Practitioner Request can be submitted by a user within a 24-hour period and to prevent duplicate payments.  While tech debt increased by 1% during the reporting period, the quarterly resiliency, cloud and customer experience goals are on target.   Investment is progressing with risks and issues that are being mitigated.

The OS OFM Commerce Business Systems (CBS) investment continues to provide an integrated financial management system that has been implemented throughout the Department of Commerce (DOC) as well as supporting G-Invoicing activities at the bureau level.  In FY24, the investment will continue in operations and maintenance with no new planned projects. Accomplishments: Investment meets functional requirements and continues to support G-Invoicing activities at bureau level, as well as implementing maintenance updates. Unique Entity Identifier:  Continued with production support.    System availability is at 100%. Help desk response time is meeting target. Investment is progressing as expected with minimal risk.

The Patents Product Line investment continues to support the Patents business by creating additional products, retiring/decommissioning more legacy systems; and supporting Patents products operational activities. Notable Accomplishments: Trained 128 users on filing in DOCX in Patent Center, driving up DOCX adoption. Enabled Plant application submission type so that applicants can permanently file electronically and reduce internal manual processing. Collaborated with PE2E Search team to identify foreign application data to improve examiner access to international patent family data. Fixed some data inconsistencies in the Workflow Management System (WMS) due to Alfresco incompatibility with AWS-Linux. Investment is progressing with risks and issues that are being mitigated.

The Trademark Product Line investment continues to maintain all Trademark legacy components across the product line and is in the process of developing modernized business and technical solutions to further improve the delivery of business value. Notable Accomplishments: After 40+ years of raw COBOL code existence, the Trademark Product Line successfully retired the TRAM (Trademark Reporting and Monitoring System) and shut down the servers; Replaced with TRM, a new, resilient, and effective replacement. Successfully deployed additional Publication Processor enhancements [Batch transaction WK03, Issue date, registration number replacement] and defect fixes. Successfully deployed TEAS changes to production to support MyUSPTO ID Me integration. Investment is progressing with some risks that are being mitigated.

investmentName: NOAA/OCIO/ NOAA R&D High Performance Computing System (HPCS)
comment: HPCS continues to be a constellation of super computers used by NOAA to perform research and development to improve climate and weather models that is meeting the mission requirements in performance.  The HPCS investment is in Operational and Maintenance mode and consistently meets and exceeds performance metrics. Accomplishments: System availability 99.59%; Data availability 100%; Compute hours made available 341,368,627. C4 retired at Oak Ridge for drop in compute hours, C6 near production to compensate in Q3. Increase in compute hours is due to allocations starting on C6. Full production in June 2024. Progressing with some risk and issues on capacity impacting the rating.

The Geographic Support Program (GSP) investment supports the integrated and automated computer-based geographic support system crucial to all censuses and household surveys. The investment continues to provide the Census address list, maps, geographic reference files, and processing systems to meet the geographic requirements of all Census Bureau programs and operations. Census counts on GSP to be able to accurately locate people and places for data collection. Accomplishments: This month GSP continues to work with the Tiger System to update and maintain the most accurate addresses and geographical information database to conduct the most accurate surveys and censuses. This month GSP Posted Cartographic Boundary File metadata to external server.  Published Generalized Service for TIGERweb.  Investment is progressing with some risk exposure.

The Central Processing investment continues to provide increased satellite network bandwidth, processing, and storage capacity. NWS is continuing to work on the impact of COVID-19 on AWIPS NAWIPS schedule and the WCOSS Transition and WCOSS Fee Liability. Accomplishments: WCOSS: Continue transition of Interactive Multi-sensor Snow and Ice Mapping System (IMS) application in support of National Ice Center. NAWIPS: PR/HFO TRR complete for High Seas Marine - Wind Wave. PR/HFO TRR complete for Tropical/CPHC. NHC Desk Flip complete for HSU Watches and Warnings. NHC ORT and Desk Flip complete for HSU GTWO. NHC Desk Flip complete for Media desk. Hazard Services:  Completed all defects that prevented sites from using the version 4 ATAN in operational mode.  AWIPS: Customer Results and Network Availability: 95.52%. Satellite Master Ground Station Availability: 100%; Met 3 out of 3 performance metrics reported. Investment is rated a 3 due to risk profile and issues.

The Dissemination investment continues to be responsible for promoting increased accessibility, interoperability, and stewardship of NOAA data, leading, delivering, and coordinating NWS contribution to NOAA, DOC, and Administration data dissemination initiatives.  Notable Accomplishments: Completed SPADES Go Live. Completed RA4-GIFs Go Live. Completed Forecast/marine.weather.gov Go Live. Matched ERMA codebase to Viewer. The investment is rated a 3 due to the risk profile and issues.

investmentName: NOAA/NESDIS/ Comprehensive Large Array-data Stewardship System (CLASS).
comment: The CLASS program continues to efficiently manage high volumes (petabytes) of satellite and in situ data and automates data ingest, quality control and access.  CLASS is the designated primary archive for most of the NOAA environmental data sets. Accomplishments: Transitioned to Operations for Release 8.3.8. Performed Release 8.3.8 COOP exercise. Added 14.76M new catalog files to the archive. Operational Availability: 97.51%. The investment is executing as expected.

Enterprise Data Lake continues to be a flexible data repository intended to provide the Census Bureau with a next generation scaling capability to fulfill data storage, reporting, analytics, and security needs while reducing costs associated with duplicative data silos. Notable Accomplishments: Multi-Account (Phase #1  EDL Core Accounts): Completed Multi account planning for remaining EDL functionality. Enterprise Data Catalog (EDC) Enhancements: Completed the Aurora shake out test in the Dev 818 account. Completed deployment and smoke test functionality to support dataset series. LakeFront Enhancements: Completed shakeout testing with Aurora database in preparation for transition to multi account. The investment is rated 3 due to risk exposure and reporting concerns.

investmentName: Census - Center for Enterprise Dissemination Services and Consumer Information (CEDSCI).
comment: The Program and the CEDSCI EDDE IT Platform project continue to be dedicated to using customer feedback to develop innovative ways to improve customer with improved data and product displays, searches, and downloads accessible from census.gov and on mobile devices. The project is in the development of a modernized platform that disseminates Census data in an efficient technological manner.  The program is responsible for both the development project plus using the new platform for disseminating Census data.  Notable Accomplishments: Launched the ability to search for geographies by address as well as the ability to download geographies as GeoJSON files on data.census.gov. Completed prototypes of new My Congressional District and My Tribal Area Landing pages. Updated schema.org metadata to improve discoverability of U.S. Census datasets. The investment continues to have a risk exposure contributing to the overall rating.

The Economic Censuses and Surveys program is a mixed life cycle investment and continues to support statistical programs that count and profile U.S. businesses and government organizations. ECON investment accomplishments include: The DIPSE Redesign team updated the EIN Unit Display for a data refresh. They also worked on test automation for Survey Unit Display and completed fixes to defects reported by UAT and QA. The AIES/SPACE team completed Data Cloning and Integration System (DCIS) Bridge/Snapshot functionality and Plain Vanilla and integrated with Mission Control. The PSIP team completed review of pre-imputation checks and imputation process. They worked on migration of post-imputation data in the stage environment. The investment is executing as expected.

investmentName: Census - Data Ingest and Collection for the Enterprise (DICE)
comment: The Data Ingest and Collection for the Enterprise (DICE) investment continues with implementing a new way of doing business that focuses on minimizing redundancy, lowering complexity, and avoiding duplicative costs for the Census's business and household data ingest and collection operations. DICE continues the efforts of being able to provide a way to collect quality data using one source. The program also continues its efforts to integrate and manage the development of an enterprise system that provides a shared platform for receiving data that has been collected by external sources, census, and survey data. Accomplishments: DICE has made strides with response rates of 30% and higher for both AIES and Special Census.  AIES-23 has been in production for a year with a response rate of 38.87%.  Special Census continues to make strides in response rates at Pingree Grove, Il and Waukee, IA and Warrenville, IL.  Investment is improving in reporting and is progressing in execution but is operating with risk exposure.

Census - The 2030 Decennial investment covers the Design Selection Phase (FYs 2022 - 2024) for the 2030 Census.  The 2030 Census strategic goals are consistent with prior decennial census goals and include: 1) A Complete and Accurate Census, 2) Embraced and Trusted Results, 3) An Efficient and Effective Program, and 4) An Appropriately Sized, Skilled, and Structured Workforce. This investment is currently in the planning phase and is on target to meet all scheduled milestones identified to date.  Accomplishments: 2026 Census Test - Baselined OD Workflow Diagram for Recruiting OD - 26CT.  Baselined OD Workflow Diagram for Selection OD - 26CT.  Baselined OD Workflow Diagram for Hiring OD - 26CT.  Solution and Operational Architecture Officially Allocate Solution Providers IPC & MQA Program Area - 26CT.  This investment is currently in the planning phase and is on target to meet all scheduled milestones identified to date. The three major areas of work in addition to general planning activities is work related to:  Design Selection, EA Research, and  The 2026 Census Test. The investment is progressing as expected.

The American Community Survey (ACS) Investment continues to support the Bureau's objective of collecting, processing, and releasing information to meet the constitutional and legislative mandates. The American Community Survey has led to a simpler decennial census, provided more timely and relevant data between censuses, and led to widespread efficiencies throughout the federal statistical system. Notable accomplishments: Completed Data Release Schedule Page for 1 Year Data Release DY 2023. Comparison Data for Detailed Tables Profiles was completed for 1 Year Review 2023. Completed PUMS Requirements Documentation for 1 Year PUMS DY 2023. The investment is progressing as expected.

BAS PMO began options document to present deployment options for NIST and Census to Department leadership. The program rating is based on replanning, risks, and continuing to work through organizational change management risks and challenges to user adoption.

investmentName: NOAA/OSC/Civilian Traffic Coordination System for Space (TraCSS)
comment: TraCSS is the Department of Commerce's enterprise solution civil space traffic coordination investment to meet Space Policy Directive 3 issued in 2018.  Directive 3 designates the Department of Commerce as the lead civilian agency for providing basic SSA data and STM services to commercial space operators.  On behalf of DOC, NOAA's Office of Space Commerce is developing the Traffic Coordination System for Space TraCSS. TraCSS will ingest, archive, process, and disseminate Space Situational Awareness (SSA) data and products for space safety and sustainability and will provide conjunction analysis and warning services to commercial satellite owner/operators. Accomplishments: Reviewing PM applications (hiring).  4 Fed TraCSS personnel onboarded (hiring). Parsons has access to DevTest environment (SI performance).  Sprints started (SI performance). The investment is progressing towards an IOC of September 2024.

The OS OFM Commerce Business Systems (CBS) investment continues to provide an integrated financial management system that has been implemented throughout the Department of Commerce (DOC) as well as supporting G-Invoicing activities at the bureau level.  In FY24, the investment will continue in operations and maintenance with no new planned projects. Accomplishments: Investment meets functional requirements and continues to support G-Invoicing activities at bureau level, as well as implementing maintenance updates. Unique Entity Identifier:  Continued with production support. System availability is at 100%. Help desk response time is meeting target. Investment is progressing as expected with minimal risk.

The Patents Product Line investment continues to support the Patents business by creating additional products, retiring/decommissioning more legacy systems; and supporting Patents products operational activities. Notable Accomplishments: Trained 145 users on filing in DOCX in Patent Center, driving up DOCX adoption. Completed decommission of EFS-Web to remove security vulnerabilities, end reliance on legacy servers and to allow retirement of co-dependent components in other business units. Made technical updates to improve monitoring of biosequence services and mitigate vulnerabilities, as well as improved reporting of search results. Implemented Auto assign for TSS OPQA reviews to automate manual tasks. Investment is progressing with risks and issues that are being mitigated.

Enterprise Product Line continues to manage all of the back-office operations including communicating with the public and employees, providing usable data collections and analytics, disseminating public records including assignment records, collecting fees, paying agency bills, supporting legal functions, providing HR capabilities, supporting budget and planning, and managing facilities and assets. Accomplishments: Completed the expansion of the journey tracking capabilities for the High Impact Service Provider (HISP) identified services allowing a 360-degree view of all USPTOs customer interactions, with reporting capabilities, across each of the USPTO HISP identified services. Progressed 50% on the integration of Customer Experience (CXM) and Customer Relationship Management (CRM) components to allow automatic capture of qualitative and quantitative information at selected points along their journey. Completed 79% Drupal content management system update of the Director's Corner blog transitioning from SharePoint, streamlines updates and enhance efficiency for blog authors. Investment is progressing with risks and issues that are being mitigated.

The Trademark Product Line investment continues to maintain all Trademark legacy components across the product line and is in the process of developing modernized business and technical solutions to further improve the delivery of business value. Notable Accomplishments: Successfully deployed Post-TRAM enhancements for ESTTA, TTABVUE, TTABIS backend, and TTABIS client. Successfully deployed release 8 - TEAS Standard Changes, Docket & Name Consent Enhancements, Color Page Revisions, CX Recommendations to the production environment. Successfully deployed Post-TRAM enhancements for ESTTA, TTABVUE, TTABIS backend, and TTABIS client. Successfully deployed Post registration functionality [Section 7, Docket Mgmt], enhancements [visual indicator in TM Viewer] to production. Investment is progressing with some risks that are being mitigated.

The Economic Censuses and Surveys program is a mixed life cycle investment and continues to support statistical programs that count and profile U.S. businesses and government organizations. ECON investment accomplishments include: The DIPSE Redesign team will continue bug fixes in Unit Acceptance Test (UAT) from previous milestones based on segment build and stage of UAT review. The AIES/SPACE team will complete DCIS Bridge/Snapshot functionality and Plain Vanilla and integrate with Mission Control. The PSIP team will draft and finalize ASPP Categorization module. The investment is executing as expected.

Enterprise Data Lake continues to be a flexible data repository intended to provide the Census Bureau with a next generation scaling capability to fulfill data storage, reporting, analytics, and security needs while reducing costs associated with duplicative data silos. Notable Accomplishments: Onboarding: Completed implementation of various requested cost savings measures for SPACE in EDL. Demo’d new S3 Mounts functionality available in EDL to SPACE. Released new Statistical Products First/Grants sub-Project workspace to users. Completed go-live of 2020 Special Census production activities. Completed provisioning for Decennial Project 111 and Non-PIKd research projects. IRE-EDL Transition: CODS continued their S3 access automation testing in the 818 account, which is expected to finish in May. The investment is rated 3 due to risk exposure and reporting concerns.

investmentName: NOAA/NESDIS/ Comprehensive Large Array-data Stewardship System (CLASS).
comment: The CLASS program continues to efficiently manage high volumes (petabytes) of satellite and in situ data and automates data ingest, quality control and access.  CLASS is the designated primary archive for most of the NOAA environmental data sets. Accomplishments: Promoted Release 8.3.7.2 to operations. Continued release planning for Release 8.3.8. Added 14.76M new catalog files to the archive. Operational Availability: 97.51%. The investment is executing as expected.

investmentName: NOAA/OCIO/ NOAA R&D High Performance Computing System (HPCS)
comment: HPCS continues to be a constellation of super computers used by NOAA to perform research and development to improve climate and weather models that is meeting the mission requirements in performance.  The HPCS investment is in Operational and Maintenance mode and consistently meets and exceeds performance metrics. Accomplishments: System availability 99.23%; Data availability 100%; Compute hours made available 330,356,736. C4 retired at Oak Ridge for drop in compute hours, C6 near production to compensate in Q3. Increase in compute hours is due to allocations starting on C6. Full production in June 2024. Progressing with some risk and issues on capacity impacting the rating.

The Geographic Support Program (GSP) investment supports the integrated and automated computer-based geographic support system crucial to all censuses and household surveys. The investment continues to provide the Census address list, maps, geographic reference files, and processing systems to meet the geographic requirements of all Census Bureau programs and operations. Census counts on GSP to be able to accurately locate people and places for data collection. Accomplishments: This month GSP posted the Cartographic boundary to the website.  These files are simplified representations of selected geographic areas on a smaller scale. Investment is progressing with some risk exposure.

The Central Processing investment continues to provide increased satellite network bandwidth, processing, and storage capacity. NWS is continuing to work on the impact of COVID-19 on AWIPS NAWIPS schedule and the WCOSS Transition and WCOSS Fee Liability. Accomplishments: WCOSS: Continued transition of Interactive Multisensor Snow and Ice Mapping System app. NAWIPS: SDM Data Requirement. NHC TRR completed for HSU GTWO.  PR/HFO PGEN test completed for High Seas Marine - Wind Wave. Hazard Services:  Completed deployment of ATAN to all participating sites.  AWIPS: Customer Results and Network Availability: 95.58. Satellite Master Ground Station Availability: 100%; Met 3 out of 3 performance metrics reported. Investment is rated a 3 due to risk profile and issues.

The Dissemination investment continues to be responsible for promoting increased accessibility, interoperability, and stewardship of NOAA data, leading, delivering, and coordinating NWS contribution to NOAA, DOC, and Administration data dissemination initiatives.  Notable Accomplishments - Digital/Graphical/Airquality sites moved to WOC (Decommissioned on NIDS).  Go Live for both NGITWS 1.3.10 and NWWS-OI. The investment is rated a 3 due to the risk profile and issues.

investmentName: Census - Data Ingest and Collection for the Enterprise (DICE)
comment: The Data Ingest and Collection for the Enterprise (DICE) investment continues with implementing a new way of doing business that focuses on minimizing redundancy, lowering complexity, and avoiding duplicative costs for the Census's business and household data ingest and collection operations. DICE continues the efforts of being able to provide a way to collect quality data using one source. The program also continues its efforts to integrate and manage the development of an enterprise system that provides a shared platform for receiving data that has been collected by external sources, census, and survey data. Accomplishments: DICE has made strides with response rates of 30% and higher for both AIES and Special Census.  AIES-23 has been in production for a year while Special Census at a 58% response rate has targeted both Pingree Grove, Il and Waukee, IA and Warrenville, IL.  CPS field Test started in March. Investment is improving in reporting and is progressing in execution but is operating with risk exposure.

investmentName: NOAA/OSC/Civilian Traffic Coordination System for Space (TraCSS)
comment: TraCSS is the Department of Commerce's enterprise solution civil space traffic coordination investment to meet Space Policy Directive 3 issued in 2018.  Directive 3 designates the Department of Commerce as the lead civilian agency for providing basic SSA data and STM services to commercial space operators.  On behalf of DOC, NOAA's Office of Space Commerce is developing the Traffic Coordination System for Space TraCSS. TraCSS will ingest, archive, process, and disseminate Space Situational Awareness (SSA) data and products for space safety and sustainability and will provide conjunction analysis and warning services to commercial satellite owner/operators. Accomplishments: PM job announcement released. Successfully provided connection to DevTest environment to pathfinder and prototype personnel. This is a new investment that is rated a 3 due to risk factors including timeline, resources, and budget.  The investment is progressing towards an IOC of September 2024.

Accomplishments: Investment meets functional requirements and continues to support G-Invoicing activities at bureau level, as well as implementing maintenance updates. investmentName: Census - Data Ingest and Collection for the Enterprise (DICE)
comment: The Data Ingest and Collection for the Enterprise (DICE) investment continues with implementing a new way of doing business that focuses on minimizing redundancy, lowering complexity, and avoiding duplicative costs for the Census's business and household data ingest and collection operations. DICE continues the efforts of being able to provide a way to collect quality data using one source. The program also continues its efforts to integrate and manage the development of an enterprise system that provides a shared platform for receiving data that has been collected by external sources, census, and survey data. Accomplishments: DICE completed milestone marks for AIES-23 with the official delivery of DICE's "MVP-1" - production Internet Self Response and Paper Data Capture capabilities and the start of data collection being carried out.  For Special Census mailed invitations went out for data collection. Investment is improving in reporting and is progressing in execution but is operating with risk exposure.

The Economic Censuses and Surveys program is a mixed life cycle investment and continues to support statistical programs that count and profile U.S. businesses and government organizations. ECON investment accomplishments include: The DIPSE Redesign team completed the first test cycle of Special Handling. The AIES/SPACE team completed production data from MOJO to CEDR - regular, automatic processing and started Rule Engine & Data Prep modules testing. The PSIP team kicked off requirements gathering weekly sessions for ASPP and is finalizing the ALFIN results in the test environment including the functionality of scheduling PSIP jobs. The investment is executing as expected.

investmentName: Census - Center for Enterprise Dissemination Services and Consumer Information (CEDSCI).
comment: The Program and the CEDSCI EDDE IT Platform project continue to be dedicated to using customer feedback to develop innovative ways to improve customer with improved data and product displays, searches, and downloads accessible from census.gov and on mobile devices. The project is in the development of a modernized platform that disseminates Census data in an efficient technological manner.  The program is responsible for both the development project plus using the new platform for disseminating Census data.  Notable Accomplishments: Completed Alpha Release of the USA Trade Application (UTA). CEDSCI is increasing their search engine optimization to find information on data.census.gov. Investment started working on a landing page to direct users to profile pages to replace the My Congressional District and My Tribal Area Landing pages.  Additional accomplishments include, 2021 ECNSVY Nonemployee Statistics, Timeseries HPS High Frequency Social and Economic Data and Timeseries ECNSVY Quarterly Summary of State and Local Tax Revenue Timeseries. The investment continues to have a risk exposure contributing to the overall rating.

investmentName: BEA Estimation Information Technology System (BEA-EITS) for Measuring the Changing US Economy.
comment: The BEA Estimation IT System encompasses BEA's core economic processing system, and directly supports BEA's mission.  This investment continues to support timely, accurate release of more than 60 critical economic estimates per year. The BEA-EITS for Measuring the Changing U.S. Economy continues to support production and dissemination of BEA's critical economic estimates as well as statistical confidentiality, including legal requirements. BEA is pursuing a Statistical Production Modernization program which seeks to simplify and modernize processes and tools by first completing business process reengineering and then updating. Accomplishments:  Supported the timely, relevant, and accurate release of eight data sets (U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services, January 2024; Trade in Value Added, 2022; U.S. International Transactions, 4th Quarter and Year 2023; Arts and Cultural Production Satellite Account, U.S. and States, 2022; U.S. International Investment Position, 4th Quarter and Year 2023; Gross Domestic Product, 4th Quarter and Year 2023 (Third Estimate), GDP by Industry, and Corporate Profits; Personal Income and Outlays, February 2024; Gross Domestic Product by State and Personal Income by State, 4th Quarter 2023 and Preliminary 2023). This investment is progressing as expected.

The agency continues to support required staffing and progress is being made filling key positions across the organization.  The NARA 801 CPIC Directive has gone through agency-wide review and will be promulgated soon.  NARA 805 SDLC is being updated to reflect current practices and clearly identify Agile processes.

All investments consider cloud first and we continue virtualization of the on-premise storage. Our multi-cloud contract (AWS, Azure and Google) continues to provide new opportunities for application development, testing and migrations to the cloud. We also continue to work on patching and maintenace in the cloud environment to support the hosting of more resources. Additionally, NARA's Data Center Modernization Project is on-schedule to complete later this year bringing the latest technology to support the Agency's increased requirements for storage and bandwidth.

Our service desk support transition to the new vendor went well. The customer service metrics continue to exceed thresholds. We continue to improve our baselines and have implemented a new hardware asset management module to assist with support and inventory. We are also working with Department of Justice on several tools for ZTA which also improve our End User Performance.

NARA revised its Federal Managers Financial Integrity Act (Material Weakness) Action Plan for IT Security to align with the Federal Information Security Management Act (FISMA) metrics and the work towards Zero Trust Architecture and meeting Executive Order (EO) 14028, Improving the Nation's Cybersecurity. All FISMA systems have a current Authority to Operate and 92% of all endpoint devices are scanned at least once every 7 days. NARA made significant progress in collecting and forwarding aggregated log information for NARA's infrastructure and various systems into our instance of Splunk with the Department of Justice and their SocAAS.

With the completion of our data circuits to the EIS contract we continue to see improved network performance and redundant internet access. We have several key projects on-going to upgrade and replace aging technology that will improve performance and minimize risk of hardware failure. Contractor resource have been increased on the support contract to assist with the design and implementation of key initiatives such as Switch Upgrades, IPv6 and Enterprise Wi-Fi.

The NextGen Catalog is operational in the production environment and considered in an O&M steady state. DAS is in O&M steady state; however, modernization and enhancement efforts for the NextGen DAS remain in progress. Final implementation and hand-off to NARA's test team is scheduled for mid-summer 2024. NextGen HMS UAT completed 03/08/24 and the production environment completed standup 03/13/24 with the production code and data. The phased rollout of the application to users was divided into four iterations beginning 03/22/24 and scheduled to end 05/13/24.

NextGen CMRS and ARCIS projects are behind schedule.  NextGen CMRS encountered requirements issues and additional development sprints for minimum viable product.  NextGen ARCIS completed the Discovery Phase and began Development this quarter, but has encountered delays.  The ERA 2.0 Program has embarked on multiple projects in the past year after selecting a new vendor for Agile development services but is working to ensure and improve consistency in performance across teams.

investmentName: OS OFM Commerce Business Applications Solution (BAS) V2
comment: The BAS program continues to modernize the Department's financial management, acquisition, and property systems.  Notable Accomplishments: Sunflower: Conducted monthly Change Network Meeting. Core Applications: Continued to resolve production issues paying travel vouchers and government purchase card transactions. Began onsite end user support at NOAA Silver Spring facility. Added additional data process support for NOAA travel voucher back log. Conducted interface requirements and design sessions. Data Warehouse: Provided Production support. The program rating is based on replanning, risks, and continues to work through organizational change management risks and challenges to user adoption.

investmentName: NOAA/OSC/Civilian Traffic Coordination System for Space (TraCSS)
comment: TraCSS is the Department of Commerce's enterprise solution civil space traffic coordination investment to meet Space Policy Directive 3 issued in 2018.  TraCSS will ingest, archive, process, and disseminate Space Situational Awareness (SSA) data and products for space safety and sustainability and will provide conjunction analysis and warning services to commercial satellite owner/operators. Accomplishments: Re-issuing vacancy announcement for PM candidates. Selected SE Lead. Establishing VPN connection to DevTest environment. Consolidated pathfinder kick off meeting and working groups formed and working out logistic details of pathfinder. This is a new investment that is rated a 3 due to risk factors including timeline, resources, and budget.  The investment is progressing towards an IOC of September 2024.

The OS OFM Commerce Business Systems (CBS) investment continues to provide an integrated financial management system that has been implemented throughout the Department of Commerce (DOC) as well as supporting G-Invoicing activities at the bureau level.  In FY24, the investment will continue in operations and maintenance with no new planned projects. Accomplishments: Investment continues to support G-Invoicing activities at bureau level, as well as implementing maintenance updates.  Investment meets functional requirements. System availability is at 100%. Help desk response time is meeting target.  All quarterly metrics met targets.  Investment is progressing as expected with minimal risk.

The Patents Product Line investment continues to support the Patents business by creating additional products, retiring/decommissioning more legacy systems; and supporting Patents products operational activities. Notable Accomplishments: Trained 385 users on filing in DOCX in Patent Center, driving up DOCX adoption. Completed Welcome Letter Phase 2 to provide applicant filer guidance through the patents process. Implemented Customized Bot Control in PPUBS to give public users a better experience in accessing the tool. Completed Highlight Text on Image for PG-Pub documents through 2024 to allow examiners an easier way to locate relevant passages in documents over the whole collection. Investment is progressing with risks and issues that are being mitigated.

The Trademark Product Line investment continues to maintain all Trademark legacy components across the product line and is in the process of developing modernized business and technical solutions to further improve the delivery of business value. Notable Accomplishments: Successfully deployed TM Notification Services (TM-NS) enhancements to production environment. Successfully deployed Trademark Status Document Retrieval (TSDR) maintenance enhancements to the production environment. Successfully deployed TRAM TTABIS services for TRAM COM replacements to the production environment. Successfully deployed TM Exam related enhancements and defect fixes to the production environment. Investment is progressing with some risks that are being mitigated.

Enterprise Product Line continues to manage all of the back-office operations including communicating with the public and employees, providing usable data collections and analytics, disseminating public records including assignment records, collecting fees, paying agency bills, supporting legal functions, providing HR capabilities, supporting budget and planning, and managing facilities and assets. Accomplishments: Legal Tools: Completed the decommissioning of the General Counsel Library System (GCLS), moving on-premises systems to the cloud and consolidating systems for increased resiliency and security. Deployed the General Counsel Case Tracking System (GCCTS) to production with updated versions of Legal Files application on new servers, Operating System and database for enhanced security and user experience. Investment is progressing with risks and issues that are being mitigated.

investmentName: NOAA/OCIO/ NOAA R&D High Performance Computing System (HPCS)
comment: HPCS continues to be a constellation of super computers used by NOAA to perform research and development to improve climate and weather models that is meeting the mission requirements in performance.  The HPCS investment is in Operational and Maintenance mode and consistently meets and exceeds performance metrics. Accomplishments: System availability 99.48%; Data availability 100%; Compute hours made available 326,424,000. R&D HPCS Program risk challenge is a capacity shortfall identified by NOAA Sci Adv 256PF is the ultimate goal to meet 100% requirement. C4 retired at Oak Ridge for drop in compute hours, C6 near production to compensate in Q3. Progressing with some risk and issues on capacity impacting the rating.

The Economic Censuses and Surveys program is a mixed life cycle investment and continues to support statistical programs that count and profile U.S. businesses and government organizations. ECON investment accomplishments include: The DIPSE Redesign team will continue bug fixes in Unit Acceptance Test (UAT) from previous milestones based on segment build and stage of UAT review. The AIES/SPACE team will start Milestone 6 to complete MOJO to CEDR, CEDR to Staging and staging to processing data flows. The PSIP team will start Annual Survey of Public Pension (ASPP) Module Milestone 1 to review existing requirements and gather ASPP requirements such as unit level imputation, item level, etc. The investment is executing as expected.

Enterprise Data Lake continues to be a flexible data repository intended to provide the Census Bureau with a next generation scaling capability to fulfill data storage, reporting, analytics, and security needs while reducing costs associated with duplicative data silos. Notable Accomplishments: Onboarding: Migrated and verified UTS interface functionality in Production. Completed various updates to SC Prod workspaces per system requests. SC PRR completed 2/20. Completed provisioning for Non-PIKd and Project 2 for 2030 Research. CAES-ACS environment build completed and handed off to project users. Multi-account (phase #1 - EDL core) planning complete to support IRE migration. Started multi-account planning for EDL Core and EDL’s tenants. The investment is rated 3 due to risk exposure and reporting concerns.

The Central Processing investment continues to provide increased satellite network bandwidth, processing, and storage capacity. NWS is continuing to work on the impact of COVID-19 on AWIPS NAWIPS schedule and the WCOSS Transition and WCOSS Fee Liability. Accomplishments: WCOSS: Continued transition of Interactive Multisensor Snow and Ice Mapping System (IMS) application in support of National Ice Center. NAWIPS: NHC TRRs complete for TAFB High Wind Graphic, HSU Watches and Warning, FEMA, and CARCAH desks. NHC ORTs complete for TAFB Surface Progs, HSU Watches and Warning, and Media desks. AWIPS: Customer Results and Network Availability: 100%; Satellite Master Ground Station Availability: 100%; Met 3 out of 3 performance metrics reported. Investment is rated a 3 due to risk profile and issues.

investmentName: NOAA/NESDIS/ Comprehensive Large Array-data Stewardship System (CLASS).
comment: The CLASS program continues to efficiently manage high volumes (petabytes) of satellite and in situ data and automates data ingest, quality control and access.  CLASS is the designated primary archive for most of NOAA environmental data sets. Accomplishments: Finished testing and Promoted Release 8.3.6.1 to operations. Completed design and implementation of Release 8.3.7. Began Release 8.3.8 requirements analysis and design.  Added 14.17M new catalog files to the archive. Operational Availability: 98.3%. The investment is executing as expected.

The Dissemination investment continues to be responsible for promoting increased accessibility, interoperability, and stewardship of NOAA data, leading, delivering, and coordinating NWS contribution to NOAA, DOC, and Administration data dissemination initiatives.  Notable Accomplishments: Completed NGITWS 1.3.9 Code Handoff.  Completed MADIS Code Handoff. Completed Alerts V2 Project. Completed IRIS/INWS 6.8.0 Code Handoff. The investment is rated a 3 due to the risk profile and issues.

investmentName: Census - Center for Enterprise Dissemination Services and Consumer Information (CEDSCI).
comment: The Program and the CEDSCI EDDE IT Platform project continue to be dedicated to using customer feedback to develop innovative ways to improve customer with improved data and product displays, searches, and downloads accessible from census.gov and on mobile devices. The project is in the development of a modernized platform that disseminates Census data in an efficient technological manner.  The program is responsible for both the development project plus using the new platform for disseminating Census data.  Notable Accomplishments: Completed Sprints 54.4 and FY24-1 at 100% and 40% of Sprint FY24-2.  Released to data.census.gov including 2022 CRE Community Resilience Estimates, 2021 CRE Community Resilience Estimates, 2020 ECNSVY Company Summary, 2020 DECIA Guam Detailed Crosstabulations, 2020 ECNSVY Characteristics of Business Owners, 2020 DECIA American Samoa Detailed Crosstabulations, 2020 DECIA U.S. Virgin Islands Detailed Crosstabulations, 2020 DECIA Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands Detailed Crosstabulations, 2019 CRE Community Resilience Estimates, Timeseries SOMA Survey of Market Absorption, and Timeseries HPS High Frequency Social and Economic Data. The investment continues to have a risk exposure contributing to the overall rating.

The Geographic Support Program (GSP) investment supports the integrated and automated computer-based geographic support system crucial to all censuses and household surveys. The investment continues to provide the Census address list, maps, geographic reference files, and processing systems to meet the geographic requirements of all Census Bureau programs and operations. Census counts on GSP to be able to accurately locate people and places for data collection. Accomplishments: GSP provided Master address file updates to all pre identified customers.  GSP uses collective participant data to process, tabulate and disseminate accurate data on behalf of the Census.  It is imperative that all data is as accurate as possible.  This month GSP sent out follow up emails to participants who had not yet responded to the Boundary and Annexation Survey.  These emails are crucial in collecting the necessary data for surveys. Investment is progressing with some risk exposure.

The 2030 Decennial investment covers the Design Selection Phase (FYs 2022 - 2024) for the 2030 Census.  The 2030 Census strategic goals are consistent with prior decennial census goals and include: 1) A Complete and Accurate Census, 2) Embraced and Trusted Results, 3) An Efficient and Effective Program, and 4) An Appropriately Sized, Skilled, and Structured Workforce. This investment is currently in the planning phase and is on target to meet all scheduled milestones identified to date.  Accomplishments: Create Initial Baseline 1 Recommendations for Project 81. 2026 Census Test - Completed Activities: Prepare and Provide Draft Stakeholder Requirements for Program Areas RQT, SPMCS & DPMO. Deliver Preliminary Findings and Recommendations for:  Tailored Contact Strategy Project to EAMT 1.1.  GQ/ETL Frame Sources.  Automating GQ and Transitory Location Operations to EAMT 2.0. Stakeholder Engagement to EAMT 2.0.  Human Resources/Onboarding Policy Decisions to EAMT 4.0. Census Integrated Personnel and Payroll System (CIPPS) to EAMT 4.0. The investment is progressing as expected.

investmentName: BEA Estimation Information Technology System (BEA-EITS) for Measuring the Changing US Economy.
comment: The BEA Estimation IT System encompasses BEA's core economic processing system, and directly supports BEA's mission.  This investment continues to support timely, accurate release of more than 60 critical economic estimates per year. The BEA-EITS for Measuring the Changing U.S. Economy continues to support production and dissemination of BEA's critical economic estimates as well as statistical confidentiality, including legal requirements. BEA is pursuing a Statistical Production Modernization program which seeks to simplify and modernize processes and tools by first completing business process reengineering and then updating. Accomplishments: Supported the timely, relevant, and accurate release of three data sets (U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services, December and Annual 2023, Gross Domestic Product, 4th Quarter and Year 2023 (Second Estimate), Personal Income and Outlays, January 2024). End User (OCS). Implemented Single Device setup for OCIO & pilot volunteers. Updated settings on BEA Conference Room displays. Network (OTS). Successfully completed N-Wave circuit failover tests. Data Center/Cloud (OTS). Completed initial discovery scan of network in development environment using ServiceNow CMDB and performed gap analysis. This investment is progressing as expected.

investmentName: Census - Data Ingest and Collection for the Enterprise (DICE)
comment: The Data Ingest and Collection for the Enterprise (DICE) investment continues with implementing a new way of doing business that focuses on minimizing redundancy, lowering complexity, and avoiding duplicative costs for the Census's business and household data ingest and collection operations. DICE continues the efforts of being able to provide a way to collect quality data using one source. The program also continues its efforts to integrate and manage the development of an enterprise system that provides a shared platform for receiving data that has been collected by external sources, census, and survey data. Accomplishments: MOJO created AIES-23 mailing workloads for NPC, QDM and Centurion. Completed releases and new CSOM/CFOMs were processed in UA. eCORR completed work on a new tool that enables users to access their survey instrument in the ITE and UAT without associating a unique email with each case. QDM and Centurion completed releases and new CSOM/CFOMs were processed in UAT. CPS delivered the SIF for all operations MIS 1, MIS 2, CAPI which MOJO successfully ingested. Investment is improving in reporting and is progressing in execution but is operating with risk exposure.

investmentName: BIS Commerce USXPORTS Exporter Support System (CUESS)
comment: The BIS CUESS investment complements the export enforcement process in support of the single IT System for the Export Control Reform directive. BIS continues to collaborate with other agencies on the USXPORTS system for multi-agency license reviews.  BIS will support the USXPORTS development for release 13.17 that improves the reliability and data efficiencies between CUESS and USXPORTS. BIS and the State Department continue to share data weekly in support of the recommendation from the GAO. Accomplishments: SNAP-R Hardening: Completed SNAP-R hardening prototype. Snowflake and Report Migration: Completed 3 Power BI dashboards for EE IMS-R reports. Completed OIG Audit report. EA Business Mapping: Collected knowledge and materials from OTE Licensing Officer Business Process Mapping effort completed so far. Purview: Resolved issue on opening labeled attachment outside domain. Enabled labeling of Power BI dashboard. APRS: Completed APRS closeout presentation and reviewed with DUS Capella. TCD Migration: Resolved all outstanding issues including performance issues. Set up PR3 application and start assessment.  Investment is progressing with risks.

The American Community Survey (ACS) Investment continues to support the Bureau's objective of collecting, processing, and releasing information to meet the constitutional and legislative mandates. The American Community Survey has led to a simpler decennial census, provided more timely and relevant data between censuses, and led to widespread efficiencies throughout the federal statistical system. Notable accomplishment:  ACS Sample Selection Period 2 Processing User Acceptance Testing for Data Year 2024 was completed. 5-Year Housing Unit (HU)and Group Quarters (GQ) Geography Files was developed for the 5-Year HU & GQ Edited Microdata Files. The investment is progressing as expected.

Notable Accomplishments: Onboarding:  Completed UTS provisioning in Production. Completed provisioning all Special Census PROD environments. Completed provisioning for Non-PIKd and Project 2 for 2030 Research. Completed provisioning of Phase 1 services for BTOS Survey's HFP Proof-of-Concept. Phase 2 is expected to begin late April. MAF/TIGER registered GRFC, GRFN, and MAFx datasets in LakeFront and delivered the most recent vintages to LakeHouse. Enterprise Data Catalog:    Deployed to Production EDC Crawler enhancements which covered the consolidation of step functions, optimization of Postgres function which moves data from stage to dimensional, and bug remediations.  Deployed to Production Logstash enhancements which covered the logic for large datasets, and logic for datasets without any datafiles Deployed to production the refactored DMS report ‘DMS Project and Datasets Used’. The investment is rated 3 due to risk exposure and reporting concerns.

investmentName: NOAA/OSC/Civilian Traffic Coordination System for Space (TraCSS)
comment: TraCSS is the Department of Commerce's enterprise solution civil space traffic coordination investment to meet Space Policy Directive 3 issued in 2018.  TraCSS will ingest, archive, process, and disseminate Space Situational Awareness (SSA) data and products for space safety and sustainability and will provide conjunction analysis and warning services to commercial satellite owner/operators. Accomplishments: Completed 3 IPTs. Cloud Provisioning completed and working on connectivity. Continued working on hiring staff including PM and System Engineer Lead. Select 2 positions for SE branch. investmentName: NOAA/NESDIS/ Comprehensive Large Array-data Stewardship System (CLASS).

Completed design and implementation of Release 8.3.7.  Cut over to AWS for dissemination.  Added 14.17M new catalog files to the archive. Operational Availability: 98.3%. The investment is executing as expected.
