Trio submitted a Breach Memorandum to Office of Program Accountability and Risk Management (PARM) in Q4 FY23, declaring a schedule and performance breach. The breach is a result of Trio?s inability to meet Key Performance Parameters (KPPs). In Q3 FY23, a Breach Remediation plan was approved with five action items to be completed by Q2 FY24. Once all action items are completed, Trio will be removed from breach. The overall Security & Privacy score is red.

The investment has provided documentation of active risk tracking via a Plan of Action & Milestones (POA&M) register. This risk documentation does not represent or track programmatic risk. Work to implement Zscaler and Okta will continue into 2024. The investment will focus on operating and maintaining OIG Security and Operations Center (SOC) services.

The investment continues to monitor a low risk to staffing. Unanticipated turnover in federal staffing positions, would affect the investment?s ability to provide proper oversight and support to OIG IT investments. To ensure that IT Management activities are not negatively impacted, the investment ensures that any staff turnover is carefully monitored and open any open positions are filled as quickly as possible.

Delivery is developing Endpoint Configuration Manager training for users. These courses will promote IT security guidelines and reduce potential security breaches. An Operational Analysis was conducted and identified that all legacy Polar Science Network equipment will be upgraded to allow for continued support and improved cybersecurity. The investment is adequately funded for FY24. Beyond FY24, the investment will be submitting requests for funding for additional staffing.

The investment has deployed a Network Operating Center (NOC) visualization solution that consolidates the performance monitoring of IT systems and security tools. The investment plans to improve worker technology options by developing policies to implement a ?Bring your Own Device? program through the utilization of a Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (VDI).

Application is piloting a Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (VDI) for remote workers. This will permit those workers to use personal devices for their government work. The program management, being in coastal Georgia, acknowledges and mitigates the identified risk of ?Climate?, referring to a probability of business interruption or facility damage due to hurricane and other weather. The recovery plan implements controls to address the potential damage that could occur to operations.

DCC has produced an evaluation guide in support of the evaluation process used to consider applications submitted for candidate systems to be migrated the cloud. The investment is managed by an Integrated Project Team (IPT), comprised of representatives from all areas of operations and management disciplines. The contract register in INVEST requires updating to reflect 2 contracts awarded during the assessment period to modernize datacenter infrastructure and reporting analytics.

Funding shortfalls remain a risk. Network does not receive enough funding to refresh network equipment, increasing the risk of downtime. Network is partially funded through fees collected from services it provides. Funding shortfalls may prevent components from paying service fees, contributing to the funding shortfall. Network is working to centralize funding to eliminate dependency on fee collection.

Supplemental funding may be required to address emerging cyber threats and requirements, such as Shadow IT. In FY24, it is anticipated that adequate funding to support Zero Trust Architecture Implementation (ZTAI) will be provided. Pending funding, the investment is on schedule to complete ZTAI by the FY24 Office of Management and Budget (OMB) suspense date. The investment has exercised the Security Operations Center (SOC) support contract to extend services through Q4 FY24.

The investment is working to address technical risks to compliance with Red Hat Enterprise Linux servers and Certified Software Asset Management controls. Additionally, work to address vulnerabilities is ongoing. EVMII was rated yellow for this assessment period on the Federal Information Security Modernization Act (FISMA) dashboard. The investment is actively preparing for an upgrade to Microsoft Windows Server 2019.

investmentName: DHS - Data Center Operations and Security
comment: The Security & Privacy section has improved to green. If end-of-life technology is not upgraded, there could be an increase in vulnerabilities. The Data Center & Cloud Optimization contractor plans to execute this upgrade but has not yet delivered a plan. Until this plan is developed and executed, this will remain a risk. Staffing is insufficient to manage operations, impacting performance. A Program Decision Option was submitted for three additional Federal positions.

In Q4 FY23, funding was secured to address shortfalls. Base funding remains inadequate, additional funding will be required in FY24 to ensure delivery of requirements and goals. Transition to Cyber Security Support Services is complete, previously delayed due to protest. Legacy contracts were extended to avoid break in service. Most staff were retained on the new contracts. The classified refresh project is funded for FY24, eliminating the backlog of hardware that was not refreshed.

Geospatial Services (GS) will experience a budget reduction in FY24. This is a risk due to increases in the number of customers using capabilities and data, as well as the increases in infrastructure and support costs. GS plans to leverage funding from Common Operating Picture and Homeland Infrastructure Foundation-Level Data. Availability is a risk due to cloud infrastructure support. This has led to outages and has delayed enhancements and patches for the system.

investmentName: DHS - CIO - National Capital Region Infrastructure Operations (NCRIO)
comment: NCRIO plans to submit the bill to FPS and OBIM for NCRIO IT services by end of Q1 FY23. NCIRO met with OCIO and the Office of the Chief Readiness Support Officer (OCRSO) to determine if changes to the current asset ownership policy were required to improve the accuracy of the services chargeback model. It was determined that no changes are required because NCRIO can assign the assets for billing purposes via actual asset ownership. The Security & Privacy section has improved to green.

Funding for modernization is a risk. The investment is limited in its ability to modernize with available funding. Resource Proposals have been deferred or denied. To mitigate shortfalls for FY24, the investment will leverage funding reserves. Requirements and Key Performance Indicators are under review by the CGCYBER and C5I Service Center divisions. Until approved, it will remain a risk. An Operational Analysis was conducted in FY23. The conclusion was modernization/replacement.

The Security & Privacy Score for the NCPS systems remained green. Early FY24, CADS program assumed responsibility for the information sharing and analytics requirements of NCPS. Current support contracts do not adequately support the processes required to deliver mission requirements. This is a risk to the program?s ability to integrate new analytic tools. A new contract award will provide a framework that will allow for an improved development environment to meet the NCPS needs.

Funding could affect the operational viability of existing fixed and movable towers and delay the implementation of new towers. Mission capability is also affected by vendor issues, causing extended repair cycles for the oldest towers. Legacy programs are most affected by maintenance issues as the older equipment has become more difficult to repair. The IST program has formed a new Integrated Product Team focused on supporting ISTs delivery of advanced capabilities to the COP program.

investmentName: DHS - Federal Protective Service (FPS) Revenue Management System (RMS)
comment: INVEST needs an update to cost and schedule for the RMS Release projects. Release 1 delays are no longer a critical issue. The contractor executed a corrective action plan to address issues impacting delivery, which was successfully delivered in Q4 FY23. Potential delays to the assessment Authority to Operate (ATO) are a low-probability risk to the program. If the ATO is delayed, the program may be unable to achieve Initial Operating Capability (IOC) by the threshold date.

The program did not meet performance metric targets. A vulnerability can cause a breach to the Federal Executive Civilian Branch, this is a risk. To mitigate, the program works to identify and respond to vulnerabilities found. Additionally, the Binding Operational Directive and the Known Exploited Vulnerability catalogue are updated to improve vulnerability detection and response. Realignment of personnel due to priorities presents a low risk to human capital.

The BECN is expected to be completed before the end of Q1 FY24. The Acquisition Program Baseline (APB) and the Life-Cycle Cost Estimate (LCCE) are being updated as part of the re-baseline. A potential funding shortfall is a risk to the program. If border security technology funding is not included in the enactment of the FY24 budget, the ongoing system modernization will be delayed. BECN ES did not meet the user satisfaction target during the most recent user survey.

Funding shortfalls will persist into FY24 as the program anticipates reduced funding. This continues to affect operations, and mission fulfillment of the MVSS program. MVSS has reduced spares inventories and is unable to replace catastrophically damaged MVSS due to funding shortfalls which create misalignment with the Acquisition Program Baseline (APB) and Operational Requirements Document (ORD) for the program.

RevMod may receive a funding reduction for FY25-26 with no funding in FY27. If this is realized, RevMod will be unable to deliver new functionalities and enhancements, impacting the investment?s ability to meet Full Operating Capability (FOC) in FY27. Multiple stakeholders are engaged to restore funding, allowing it to reach FOC and move into sustainment by FY28. In Q1 FY24, RevMod integrated with ACE Collections. ACE Collections is now the system of record for CBP collections.

Updates to the Acquisition Program Baseline and Life-Cycle Cost Estimates have been delayed to Q1 FY24 pending the BECN ES re-baseline. These will reflect plans to extend the lifecycle and migration of legacy systems in CBP Amazon Web Services Cloud Environment (CACE). Operating legacy systems in a cloud environment may increase costs for the investment. To mitigate, the program will work with the Office of Information Technology (OIT) to monitor cloud strategy, requirements, and costs.

GMM successfully achieved Acquisition Decision Event (ADE) 3 Q4 FY23 and is on schedule to complete all requirements for Full Operating Capability (FOC) before the end of Q2 FY24. Failed transactions have imposed a significant strain on development resources. This is a risk to the program. A system integration support contract is planned for award in Q2 FY24. A new contract for system integration and application development support is planned that will extend services through Q2 FY24.

The LCCE update is ongoing, to be completed by the end of Q1 FY24, which will more accurately reflect the current funding profile. The Security and Privacy score for this assessment period has improved to green. Efforts to separate microservices, for more efficient development, continue to progress with the program focusing on the next step, which is creating a common user interface for separated services. Defect management and process improvement also remain a focus for development.

The merger of the NII program and NII-I funding is a risk which includes requirements definition, staffing, and AI/integration, notably identifying commercially available Anomaly Detection Algorithms, and development resources. The program expects to achieve ADE-2B in FY26 with deployments of AI equipment and components as those capabilities mature. Deployment of Multi-Energy Portals and Low-Energy Portals has been impacted by funding shortfalls due to increases in construction costs.

All investments consider cloud first and we continue virtualization of the on-premise storage.  Our multi-cloud contract (AWS, Azure and Google) continues to provide new opportunities for application development, testing and migrations to the cloud.  We also continue to work on patching and maintenace in the cloud environment to support the hosting of more resources.  Additionally NARA is undertaking new efforts to upgrade our data center.

Our service desk support continues to improve and the customer service measurements remain above 90%.  We continue to improve our baselines and have implemented a new hardware asset management tool to assist with support and inventory.  We are also working with Department of Justice on several tools for ZTA which also improve our End User Performance.

NARA made significant progress addressing open audit recommendations and closing actions within the self-declared Material Weaknesses (MW).  Due to the change in cybersecurity priorities, the MW was restructured to align with the five Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) pillars to better track progress on required actions.  The restructuring of the IT Security Methodologies was also completed in which 20 methodology documents were replaced by 5 handbooks.  NARA has improved patching capabilities through the use of auto-updates for common standard products and implementation of Microsoft SCCM.

The agency continues to support required staffing and progress is being made filling key positions across the organization.  The NARA 801 CPIC Directive has gone through agency-wide review and will be promulgated soon.  NARA 805 SDLC is being updated to reflect current practices and clearly identify Agile processes.

While improvements have been made, there is still Network risk. We have completed the transition of data circuits to the EIS contract improving performance and providing redundant internet access.  We have procured new hardware and initiating projects to upgrade and replace aging technology to improve performance.  Once the transition to a new IT support contractor is complete, we will have increased contract resources to assist with the design and implementation of key initiatives such as VoIP, IPv6 and Enterprise Wi-Fi.

The NextGen Catalog is now operational in the production environment and considered in an O&M steady state. The legacy NAC is scheduled to be decommissioned by December 2023. DAS is in O&M steady state; however, modernization and enhancement efforts for the NextGen DAS remain in progress. There is a delay in the NextGen DAS final release due to product and sprint backlog replanning, redefined service level agreements (SLAs), and underestimation of level of effort (LOE). In addition, NARA's transition from SecureAuth to Azure AD has caused an additional shift in schedule, final delivery date and costs due to the LOE for the vendor to implement.  NextGen HMS has completed the developement phase of the project.  UAT and Stage Gate reviews will run through December 2023 and rollout and data migration is projected to occur during Q1 CY 2024.

NextGen CMRS has four remaining development sprints and is projected to go-live at the beginning of CY 2024. NextGen ARCIS is in the beginning phase of a 20-month project.  The IPT meets weekly on these projects, which support the NISP Modernization efforts.  The ERA 2.0 Program rolled out the scheduling and transfer components to all Federal Agencies and is now addressing migration errors and required infrastructure upgrades.  In addition, foundational work for integrating with the NextGen Description & Authority Service (DAS) and providing Access Review & Redaction capabilities for ERA 2.0 has begun. This required onboarding and orienting additional vendor Agile teams.  The team is also adopting a new Agile release process allowing us to release new code monthly instead of the current quarterly cadence.

investmentName: CISA - Information Technology Security and Compliance (ITSC)
comment: CISA has completed its efforts to ensure all systems are monitored by a Security Operation Center. Progress continues for CISA?s effort to migrate these services to the Network Operations and Security Center. The investment has continued to focus on efforts to identify and document core systems as they become aware of these systems to ensure continuous system monitoring across the enterprise. The overall security and privacy score is green.

Changes to the Binding Operational Directive (BOD) has allowed the investment to better address BODs; allowing the investment to better meet vulnerability compliance targets. The investment continues to deliver updates and patches to workstations and applications; patches have been on schedule and compliance targets have been met. A new contract was awarded in Q4 FY23 without staff turnover. The Integrated Project Team charter has been updated, establishing a biannual review meeting.

The program will resume application and database cloud migrations in FY24, as cloud environments become available to accommodate these migrations. The program reports that while there are past delays in migrations, these delays have not presented any hardware End-of-Life (EOL) issues, but EOL remains a risk. The program plans to migrate the Test and Development Lab and resume stand up of infrastructure and rehosting of application and databases to the new Azure and Oracle Environments.

investmentName: FEMA - Data Center - Emergency Operations Center ITSC & Cloud
comment: Data Center continues to experience delays in migrating applications to the cloud, exposing a risk of aging hardware. The primary mitigation is the on-going effort to move eligible applications from FEMA Gov Data Center facility to the cloud. The program has continued the plan and prepare for the migration of applications and systems to the cloud and provided recommended courses of action to the CIO. The overall security and privacy score is red.

The Cloud Migration project is now on hold pending a reassessment of options for the ECC system. An alternatives analysis will be conducted to determine options that may deliver benefits of the cloud migration with limited cost. The investment has opted to virtualize NAC infrastructure to allow for software upgrades and reduce amount of hardware, this virtualization is on schedule to be completed by Q1 FY24. The overall security and privacy score is green.

Funding has remained a risk to the investment, lack of funding has prevented the transition of the training programs to a properly approved platform. With the transition of Accessibility to the new Customer Experience Directorate (CXD), the program will define new goals for the Accessibility and Language Services Division. Activities of Accessibility are currently focused on adapting to changes following the CXD realignment.

investmentName: DHS - Environmental Planning and Historic Preservation Decision Support System
comment: Funding gaps going into FY24 imposes increased risk for performance and support activities. The cloud migration is expected to begin in Q2 FY24 however that is dependent on the available funding and the Solutions Development Directorate?s migration timeline. A continued state of insufficient funds is forecasted which will lead to reduction in support, resources, and extend delivery schedules.

Funding and human resource gaps have been mitigated by repurposing internal funding and utilization of matrixed staff, however additional funding is needed. Regional expansion projects have not experienced any additional delays since the schedules noted during the last Assessment. Circuit delivery and installation delays remain a risk, supply chain shortages affect the program?s ability to maintain schedule for ongoing regional expansion. The overall security and privacy score is red.

investmentName: DHS - CIO - Identity Credential and Access Management (ICAM)
comment: Forest trust is a component of Active Directory (AD) and enables collaboration with all DHS AD systems for all Components and legacy authentication. The decommissioning of forest trust remains a risk, due to a potential increase in security vulnerabilities. The investment is working with to ensure Components transition away from forest trust. Full funding is expected for FY24, with no existing or projected funding shortfalls. The security and privacy score has improved to green.

The Enrollment System and Credential Modernization project faces a condensed schedule due to a previous protest of the contract award. As a result, the investment has established daily meetings with the contractor to develop an Integrated Master Schedule that will identify resources, scope, and a deployment schedule to meet the target Q1 FY25 deadline. The overall security and privacy score is green.

investmentName: DHS - CIO - Homeland Secure Data Network (HSDN)
comment: Inadequate funding remains a moderate risk to the program. If adequate funding is not received, the program may be unable to sustain operations due to user count increases and ensure timely compliance with National Security Memorandom-8. The program has submitted Unfunded Requests for additional funding to meet these requirements. A manpower analysis is planned to identify staffing deficiencies and to suggest courses of action for additional federal staff and contractor support.

New initiatives have diverted some program resources, delaying the React migration, which remains a risk. An update to support the DACA rebuild development has been completed and deployed to production in Q4 FY23. Action to prevent future outages was taken to fix the root cause of ELIS missing a performance metric due to a number of outages. Interviews are currently being conducted for vacancies, with announcements expected Q1 FY24. The overall security and privacy score is green.

investmentName: DHS - CIO - Homeland Security Information Network (HSIN)
comment: The HSIN Modernization Project will replace the current system with a modern cloud solution. This modernization effort is ongoing and is adequately funded. A new program manager is pursuing the certification required for this investment. SecDevOps is integrated at each level of development to mitigate risks associated with implementation of new user requirements and future technology upgrades. The overall security and program score is green.

investmentName: FEMA - Logistics Supply Chain Management System (LSCMS)
comment: The transition to FEMA Cloud Access Point was completed in Q3 FY23. The transition has improved system latency, availability, troubleshooting capabilities, and usage visibility. In Q4 FY23, the investment completed the monthly cybersecurity patches to ensure the security posture of the operational system, and deployed the Trailer Management functionality which allows trailers to be tracked in LSCMS throughout the trailer?s lifecycle. The overall security and privacy score is green.

Funding was received to exercise option years on service contracts for operations and sustainment. The program continues to track a funding risk, future funding reductions in operations and sustainment or procurement, construction, and improvement may impact development, operations, and contract awards. RAVEN has submitted a funding request to leadership for additional staff and resources to support new initiatives. The overall security and privacy score remains yellow.

Previous funding risks impacting full operational capability schedule thresholds have been mitigated. The requirements have been decoupled from the technology modernization funding, mitigating risk of delayed fund disbursements. The final procurement, construction, and improvement funding allotment was received in Q3 FY23, mitigating previously identified schedule risk. The phase 4 project is on schedule for completion by end of Q1 FY24. The overall security and privacy score is green.

Funding continues to be a risk while performing IDENT operations, the program and leadership are actively pursuing additional funding. The program is actively addressing vulnerabilities which include EOL components which keep the overall security of the system low. HART security and privacy score is red for this assessment period.

IDENT can be retired when HART reaches IOC, thus delays to the IOC schedule presents a risk. HART has requested funds for continued IDENT operations while progress towards IOC continues. HART?s program manager and PMO will be directly reporting to the Chief Information Officer in the future; the impacts of transitioning IDENT resources to support HART will need to be further assessed once a decision is reached.

The program is monitoring key performance parameter achievement to ensure suitability for United States Border Patrol. A contract rework is ongoing in support of increasing capabilities, no breaks in service are expected. The overall security and privacy score improved to yellow.

TIM is on track with improving resilience, survivability, and disaster recovery capabilities of the vetting and credentialing system (VCS). RISKS: USAID has achieved significant advances in addressing cybersecurity risks and meeting unanticipated challenges that COVID-19 placed on the Agency's IT infrastructure. As the Agency moves forward and expands development authorization to locally led staff, the reliance on IT systems and infrastructure to securely deliver information anytime and anywhere faces even greater pressure and challenges. Additionally, recent events including Russia's invasion of Ukraine coupled with a need to respond to cyber-attacks, disinformation and threats to USAID's overseas operations and partners has resulted in an increased cybersecurity and privacy risk to the Agency, the Nation, and its allies. MITIGATION: These risks can be mitigated through continued investment in both emerging technologies and compliance driven by Federal law, regulation and policy. Technology advancements include Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) that enable predictive defense and automated remediation that, when combined with an emphasis in cyber security and privacy compliance, allow USAID to a) provide an automated and often preemptive response to the latest threats, regulations, mandates, and technical advancements; and b) increase efficiency and effectiveness of Cybersecurity Framework functions and privacy controls that are critical to maintaining cyber hygiene and risk management and are audited by various entities like OIG, GAO and other oversight entities.

comment: The BAS program continues to modernize the Department's financial management, acquisition, and property systems.  Notable Accomplishments: Core Applications: Began PRISM, EBS, and Sunflower training. Continued UAT for BAS PMO users (Wave 1E, 1F and 1G). Provided support for UAT users; addressed bugs found in testing. Data Warehouse: Continued Regression testing. Conducted data validation. The program rating is based on replanning, risks, and continues to work through organizational change management risks and challenges to user adoption.

investmentName: NOAA/OCIO/ NOAA R&D High Performance Computing System (HPCS)
comment: HPCS is a constellation of super computers used by NOAA to perform research and development to improve climate and weather models that is meeting the mission requirements in performance.  The HPCS investment is in Operational and Maintenance mode and constituently meets and exceeds performance metrics. Accomplishments: System availability 99.53%; Data availability 100%; Compute hours made available 406,369,059. Currently approaching 30PF of available HPC.C5 (Gaea) in production at Oak Ridge. Progressing with some risk and issues on capacity impacting the rating.  The Human Capital risk is being addressed and partially mitigated.

investmentName: NOAA/OSC/Civilian Traffic Coordination System for Space (TraCSS)
comment: TraCSS is the Department of Commerce's enterprise solution civil space traffic coordination investment to meet Space Policy Directive 3 issued in 2018.  TraCSS will ingest, archive, process, and disseminate Space Situational Awareness (SSA) data and products for space safety and sustainability and will provide conjunction analysis and warning services to commercial satellite owner/operators. Accomplishments: Expedited ramp up of program, acquisitions and coordination with DoD and external stakeholders.  This is a new investment and initially being rated as a 3 due to risk factors including timeline, resources, and budget.

The Dissemination investment continues to be responsible for promoting increased accessibility, interoperability, and stewardship of NOAA data, leading, delivering, and coordinating NWS contribution to NOAA, DOC, and Administration data dissemination initiatives.  Notable Accomplishments: Go Live of GIS National Viewer 2.1. NWSChat 2.0 became operational. Completion of Southern Region Modernization Project. Completion of DAT upgrade from 10.8.1 to 11.0.1. Completion of RIDGE 2 upgrade.  The investment is rated a 3 due to the risk profile and issues.

Enterprise Data Lake continues to be a flexible data repository intended to provide the Census Bureau with a next generation scaling capability to fulfill data storage, reporting, analytics, and security needs while reducing costs associated with duplicative data silos. Notable Accomplishments: Onboarding~ IRE > EDL Migration data transfer, verification, and user access design and prototyping in progress with CODS. Two additional 2030 projects environments were released and began onboarding process with two others.  One additional Continuous Count Study environment released. Finalizing late requests for SC TRR3 (including changes to DAS interface and additional access for project level team members) provisioning and working through TRR4 provisioning. The investment is rated 3 due to risk exposure and reporting concerns.

The Central Processing investment continues to provide increased satellite network bandwidth, processing, and storage capacity. NWS is continuing to work on the impact of COVID-19 on AWIPS NAWIPS schedule and the WCOSS Transition and WCOSS Fee Liability. Accomplishments: WCOSS: Continue transition of Interactive Multisensor Snow and Ice Mapping System (IMS) app. NAWIPS: NHC TAFB Wind Wave Product now fully operations in AWIPS-2. Complete NHCTAFB Danger Graphic PGEN. AWIPS: Customer Results and Network Availability: 97.5%; Satellite Master Ground Station Availability: 100%; Met 3 out of 3 performance metrics reported. Rated 3 due to risk profile and issues.

investmentName: NOAA/NESDIS/ Comprehensive Large Array-data Stewardship System (CLASS).
comment: The CLASS program continues to efficiently manage high volumes (petabytes) of satellite and in situ data and automates data ingest, quality control and access.  CLASS is the designated primary archive for most of NOAA environmental data sets. Accomplishments: Completed initial Release 8.3.5 Implementation and test case creation.  Began Release 8.3.5 Testing. Promote Release 8.3.5 into Operations. Added 16.7M new catalog files to the archive. Operational Availability: 97.85%. The investment is executing as expected.

The Economic Censuses and Surveys program is a mixed life cycle investment and continues to support statistical programs that count and profile U.S. businesses and government organizations. ECON investment accomplishments include: The DIPSE Redesign team completed development of Duplicate Review Display Tool and completed updates to Affiliation Sold. The AIES/SPACE team completed EDL on-boarding to access various AWS services and SPACE database infrastructure (Redshift and Postgres).  The SPACE software development team also completed database design performance benchmarking and API endpoints for correction screen, then they deployed rule engine within Census boundary.  The PSIP team completed the methodology design and development of the debt calculation logic. The investment is executing as expected.

The Geographic Support Program (GSP) investment supports the integrated and automated computer-based geographic support system crucial to all censuses and household surveys. The investment continues to provide the Census address list, maps, geographic reference files, and processing systems to meet the geographic requirements of all Census Bureau programs and operations. Accomplishments: Delivered SAS Master Address File Extract files to pre-identified customers. Delivered Spatial and Address Data Dump Files to customer for Listing and Mapping Address (LIMA). The investment is progressing with a risk exposure.

The 2030 Decennial investment covers the Design Selection Phase (FYs 2022 - 2024) for the 2030 Census.  The 2030 Census strategic goals are consistent with prior decennial census goals and include: 1) A Complete and Accurate Census, 2) Embraced and Trusted Results, 3) An Efficient and Effective Program, and 4) An Appropriately Sized, Skilled, and Structured Workforce. This investment is currently in the planning phase and is on target to meet all scheduled milestones identified to date.  Accomplishments: Completed Baseline Program Test and Evaluation Management Plan with signatures.  Completed Baseline the Strategic Management Plan with signatures. The investment is progressing as expected.

investmentName: BEA Estimation Information Technology System (BEA-EITS) for Measuring the Changing US Economy.
comment: The BEA Estimation IT System encompasses BEA's core economic processing system, and directly supports BEA's mission.  This investment continues to support timely, accurate release of more than 60 critical economic estimates per year. The BEA-EITS for Measuring the Changing U.S. Economy continues to support production and dissemination of BEA's critical economic estimates as well as statistical confidentiality, including legal requirements. BEA is pursuing a Statistical Production Modernization program which seeks to simplify and modernize processes and tools by first completing business process reengineering and then updating. Accomplishments: Implemented two Citrix NetScaler firmware updates to maintain compliance and protect against zero-day attacks. The prototype was deployed to a testing group. Implemented Web Application Firewall rules in the to-be web environment.  Prepared to-be web environment for expanded performance and penetration testing. This investment is progressing as expected.

investmentName: Census - Data Ingest and Collection for the Enterprise (DICE)
comment: The Data Ingest and Collection for the Enterprise (DICE) investment continues with implementing a new way of doing business that focuses on minimizing redundancy, lowering complexity, and avoiding duplicative costs for the Census's business and household data ingest and collection operations. DICE continues the efforts of being able to provide a way to collect quality data using one source. The program also continues its efforts to integrate and manage the development of an enterprise system that provides a shared platform for receiving data that has been collected by external sources, census, and survey data. Accomplishments: The AIES-DR production workload delivered to the NPC (via MOJO OCS) to enable the preparation of invitation. Centurion Penetration Testing completed and ATO. Completed TRR-3 testing. Investment is improving in reporting and is progressing in execution but is operating with a risk exposure.

investmentName: BIS Commerce USXPORTS Exporter Support System (CUESS)
comment: The BIS CUESS investment complements the export enforcement process in support of the single IT System for the Export Control Reform directive. BIS continues to collaborate with other agencies on the USXPORTS system for multi-agency license reviews.  BIS will support the USXPORTS development for release 13.17 that improves the reliability and data efficiencies between CUESS and USXPORTS. BIS and the State Department continue to share data weekly in support of the recommendation from the GAO. Accomplishments: Addressed enhancement request from OAC to update the forms BIS-621P and BIS-6051P-a on the BIS website to include a new 'Boycotting Entity' field. The BIS Consolidated screening list contains data through June 30. The investment is progressing with risks. The BIS-AES analytical data from CBP has been updated to the June baseline with 4.8m records. The BIS Consolidated screening list contains data through July 26. BIS supported requests from USXPORTS and developed monitoring report for application referrals. Implemented Snowflake data analytics environment architecture Phase 1 and implemented the interface with MITRE to improve BIS administration. The investment is progressing with risks.

investmentName: Census - Center for Enterprise Dissemination Services and Consumer Information (CEDSCI).
comment: The Program and the CEDSCI EDDE IT Platform project are dedicated to using customer feedback to develop innovative ways to improve customer with improved data and product displays, searches, and downloads accessible from census.gov and on mobile devices. The project is in the development of a modernized platform that disseminates Census data in an efficient technological manner.  The program is responsible for both the development project plus using the new platform for disseminating Census data.  Notable Accomplishments: Completed Sprints 51.1 and 51.2 100% and 58% of Sprint 51.3.  Released 9 datasets to data.census.gov. The investment continues to have a risk exposure contributing to the overall rating.

The American Community Survey (ACS) Investment continues to support the Bureau's objective of collecting, processing, and releasing information to meet the constitutional and legislative mandates. The American Community Survey has led to a simpler decennial census, provided more timely and relevant data between censuses, and led to widespread efficiencies throughout the federal statistical system. Notable accomplishment: Completed production of ACS 2022 1-year files and began verification. Completed the start of the tabulation for ACS 2018-2022 5-year estimates. Completed the internal review on ACS 2018-2022 5-year estimates. Completed the comprehensive guide for ACS Data Products. The investment is progressing as expected.

Hiring for permanent full-time staff are underway. The FEMADex Authority to Proceed has been approved. This will allow the system to connect to FEMA source systems and data. The program continues to work with Data Enablement to ensure existing policy and functionality of the new system are in alignment.

TECS Mod received yellow scores on the final FISMA scorecard. The migration of infrastructure from CentOS to the new Red Hat Enterprise Linux has been delayed. CentOS is past End of Life leading to an increased risk of vulnerabilities. The Full Operational Capability release of the Digital Records Management Module was completed in Q3 FY23. The release provides an electronic media solution to users. This is compliant with a National Archives and Records Administration mandate.

Cost and schedule uncertainty of the migration to the CBP Amazon Web Services Cloud US East (CACE) remains a risk. If changes to application components or database configurations are identified, the cost and schedule of the migration effort may exceed estimates. Migration to the CACE is nearing completion. All application components are on target to be operational in production CACE environments by Q4 FY23. The database migration will begin in Q1 FY24 and conclude before the end of FY24.

To be compliant with cybersecurity guidelines, the Office of Information Technology determined a replacement for switches is needed to reduce the risk of security vulnerabilities. Currently, testing is being conducted to determine the most efficient and effective replacement. LBI will continue to monitor this risk until a switch replacement is determined, funded, procured, and installed. The investment will continue to refresh funded legacy lane technology through FY23.

HRIT received a red rating in the final FISMA scorecard. The Learning system solution has been offline and will not be restored as the vendor hosting site has experienced continuing hardware failure. This issue leaves DHS without a training system for mandatory training. The program plans to stand up the Hiring Information Tracking System in Q4 FY23 as an interim solution. The operational challenges of the learning system has halted its services across DHS.

The Base Station Replacement project will replace obsolete hardware that does not allow for the full transmission of safety messages, so that safety messages are provided in near real-time. NAIS investment an Engineering Tailoring Plan that includes changes to the BSR requirements. Once approve, NAIS will establish cost and schedule baselines. USCG Office of Capabilities is developing a new Operational Analysis for the NAIS investment, to be completed by Q3 FY23.

Secure Flight received a red rating on the final FISMA scorecard. The investment has completed all equipment refreshes at the Colorado Springs center but has not refreshed all desktop equipment at the Annapolis Junction center. The refresh is intended to improve the efficiency of the review process that is performed by analysts on select passengers. In the interim, the SMO has developed a plan for a temporary equipment solution that will be procured and tested by the end of Q4 FY23.

The Economic Censuses and Surveys program is a mixed life cycle investment and continues to support statistical programs that count and profile U.S. businesses and government organizations. ECON investment accomplishments include: The DIPSE Redesign team completed development of Allocate Payment and Payroll and continued the development of Duplicate Review Display Tool. The AIES/SPACE team completed database design performance benchmarking and continued UI functional and design updates including correction screen data tables, and user preferences from any device or browser. The PSIP completed creating the draft of requirements with few action items to finalize and started testing the cell categorization. The investment is executing as expected.

The American Community Survey (ACS) Investment continues to support the Bureau's objective of collecting, processing, and releasing information to meet the constitutional and legislative mandates. The American Community Survey has led to a simpler decennial census, provided more timely and relevant data between censuses, and led to widespread efficiencies throughout the federal statistical system. Notable accomplishment: Completed tabulation software testing on revised applications and systems. Completed release of the ACS 2017-2021 5-year SPT/AIAN estimates. Completed the submission of the ACS 2022 1-year Public Use Microdata Sample (PUMS) requirements, data dictionary, and release package to Disclosure Review Board (DRB) for approval. Completed production of the ACS 2022 1-year estimates and review tools. The investment is progressing as expected.

Enterprise Data Lake continues to be a flexible data repository intended to provide the Census Bureau with a next generation scaling capability to fulfill data storage, reporting, analytics, and security needs while reducing costs associated with duplicative data silos. Notable Accomplishments: Onboarding: Finished Special Census and AIES UAT setup IRE EDL Migration data transfer, verification, and user access design and prototyping in progress with CODS. Lakefront: Testing for Phase 1 enhancements deployed to PROD on June 26 post the metadata catalog (EDC) population in PROD.  Enterprise Data Catalog (EDC):  Deployed the EDC custom crawler to production, extending the crawling framework to capture technical metadata for AWS Glue unsupported file types. Deployed to production a framework to support Ad-Hoc EDC Registration and the retroactive cataloging of existing DMS datasets loaded. The investment is rated 3 due to risk exposure and reporting concerns.

investmentName: Census - Data Ingest and Collection for the Enterprise (DICE)
comment: The Data Ingest and Collection for the Enterprise (DICE) investment continues with implementing a new way of doing business that focuses on minimizing redundancy, lowering complexity, and avoiding duplicative costs for the Census's business and household data ingest and collection operations. DICE continues the efforts of being able to provide a way to collect quality data using one source. The program also continues its efforts to integrate and manage the development of an enterprise system that provides a shared platform for receiving data that has been collected by external sources, census, and survey data. Accomplishments: Released UAT plan and started the UAT for the DICE MVP surveys (Annual Integrated Economic Survey, Special Census). Finalized CPS Modernization plan. Complete all planned development for TRR-3. Investment is improving in reporting and is progressing in execution but is operating with a risk exposure.

The Geographic Support Program (GSP) investment supports the integrated and automated computer-based geographic support system crucial to all censuses and household surveys. The investment continues to provide the Census address list, maps, geographic reference files, and processing systems to meet the geographic requirements of all Census Bureau programs and operations. Accomplishments: Delivered Geographic Reference File Codes and Names test files and notified pre-identified customers. Delivered Master Address File Extract Test files and notified pre-identified customers. Census count on GSP to be able to accurately locate people and places for data collection. The investment is progressing with a risk exposure.

investmentName: Census - Center for Enterprise Dissemination Services and Consumer Information (CEDSCI).
comment: The Program and the CEDSCI EDDE IT Platform project are dedicated to using customer feedback to develop innovative ways to improve customer with improved data and product displays, searches, and downloads accessible from census.gov and on mobile devices. The project is in the development of a modernized platform that disseminates Census data in an efficient technological manner.  The program is responsible for both the development project plus using the new platform for disseminating Census data.  Notable Accomplishments: Completed 100% of program increment 50 and started program increment 51 (10%).  Released 21 datasets to data.census.gov. The investment continues to have a risk exposure contributing to the overall rating.

The 2030 Decennial investment covers the Design Selection Phase (FYs 2022 - 2024) for the 2030 Census.  The 2030 Census strategic goals are consistent with prior decennial census goals and include: 1) A Complete and Accurate Census, 2) Embraced and Trusted Results, 3) An Efficient and Effective Program, and 4) An Appropriately Sized, Skilled, and Structured Workforce. This investment is currently in the planning phase and is on target to meet all scheduled milestones identified to date.  Accomplishments: Continued developing management plans and preparing for data availability testing. The investment is progressing as expected.

investmentName: OS OFM Commerce Business Applications Solution (BAS) V2
comment: The BAS program continues to modernize the Department's financial management, acquisition, and property systems.  Notable Accomplishments: Core Applications: Completed UAT for BAS PMO users (Wave 1B, 1C and 1D). Began UAT for NOAA users (Waves 1B, 1C). Provided support for UAT users; addressed bugs found in testing. Data Warehouse: Completed system and integration testing for EDW. Began Regression testing. Completed EDW training materials. The program rating is based on replanning and risks and continues to work through organizational change management risks and challenges to user adoption.

The OS OFM Commerce Business Systems (CBS) investment continues to provide an integrated financial management system that has been implemented throughout the Department of Commerce (DOC) as well as supporting G-Invoicing activities at the bureau level.  In FY23, the investment is in operations and maintenance with no new planned projects. Accomplishments: G-Invoicing:  Continued production support of G-Invoicing activities at the bureau level, as well as implementing updates. Unique Entity Identifier:  Continued with production support. The investment meets functional requirements. System availability is at 99.84%. The investment is progressing as expected with minimal risk.

The Patents Product Line investment continues to support the Patents business by creating additional products; retiring/decommissioning more legacy systems; and supporting Patents products operational activities. Notable Accomplishments: Trained 22,550 users to date on filing in DOCX in Patent Center, increasing Patent Center and DOCX usage. Completed Patent Center Rocky Linux Phase 1 migration to remove Red Hat dependency. Added integration points to the Global Dossier in the Docket and Application Viewer (DAV) to facilitate finding patent family citation data and increase access to prior art. The investment is progressing with risks and issues that are being mitigated.

The Trademark Product Line investment continues to maintain all Trademark legacy components across the product line and is in the process of developing modernized business and technical solutions to further improve the delivery of business value. Notable Accomplishments Successfully deployed Electronic Official Gazette (eOG) Publication Services to production environment. Successfully deployed eSignature capability to production environment. Successfully deployed TELCO related TRAM transactions (6009 and EC01) as part of the retirement effort to the production environment. The investment is progressing with some risks and issues that are being mitigated.

Enterprise Product Line continues to manage all of the back-office operations including communicating with the public and employees, providing usable data collections and analytics, disseminating public records including assignment records, collecting fees, paying agency bills, supporting legal functions, providing HR capabilities, supporting budget and planning, and managing facilities and assets. Accomplishments: CCX - Completed PTOWeb enhancements: Business Unit roles, announcement functionality, calendar and events improvements, floating Point of Contact footer, and the ability for anonymous users to view published content. Successfully moved the Image Gallery component of PTOWeb cloud; deployed MyUSPTO R4.21 to provide enhanced logging for better data traceability. Completed the annual assessment for the Intellectual Property Leadership Management Support System. The investment is progressing with risks and issues that are being mitigated.

investmentName: BIS Commerce USXPORTS Exporter Support System (CUESS)
comment: The BIS CUESS investment complements the export enforcement process in support of the single IT System for the Export Control Reform directive. BIS continues to collaborate with other agencies on the USXPORTS system for multi-agency license reviews.  BIS will support the USXPORTS development for release 13.17 that improves the reliability and data efficiencies between CUESS and USXPORTS. BIS and the State Department continue to share data weekly in support of the recommendation from the GAO. Accomplishments: added new OCC Attorneys to CMT; updated IMS-R field office in Screen Review for agent transferee; actively loading data into Snowflake daily; and added Juneteenth as a Federal holiday in CUESS. The BIS Automated Export System analytical data from CBP has been updated to the May baseline with 4.6m records. The BIS Consolidated screening list contains data through June 30. The investment is progressing with risks.

The Dissemination investment continues to be responsible for promoting increased accessibility, interoperability, and stewardship of NOAA data, leading, delivering, and coordinating NWS contribution to NOAA, DOC, and Administration data dissemination initiatives.  Notable Accomplishments: Completed Ridge 2 Code Handoff. Completed deployment of NWS Internal users into NWSChat 2.0. Completed sunset of IDP-GIS and Redirect IDP-GIS to CloudGIS. Completed Weather.gov 2.0 Path Analysis. Go Live of GMDSS.  The investment is rated a 3 due to the risk profile and issues.

The Central Processing investment continues to provide increased satellite network bandwidth, processing, and storage capacity. NWS is continuing to work on the impact of COVID-19 on AWIPS NAWIPS schedule and the WCOSS Transition and WCOSS Fee Liability. Accomplishments: WCOSS: Continued transition of Interactive Multi-sensor Snow and Ice Mapping System (IMS) application in support of National Ice Center. NAWIPS: Completed WPC Desk ORT. SAB PGEN readiness completed. AWIPS: Customer Results and Network Availability: 97.1%; Satellite Master Ground Station Availability: 100%; Met 3 out of 3 performance metrics reported. Rated 3 due to risk profile and issues.

investmentName: BEA Estimation Information Technology System (BEA-EITS) for Measuring the Changing US Economy.
comment: The BEA Estimation IT System encompasses BEA's core economic processing system, and directly supports BEA's mission.  This investment supports timely, accurate release of more than 60 critical economic estimates per year. The BEA-EITS for Measuring the Changing U.S. Economy supports production and dissemination of BEA's critical economic estimates as well as statistical confidentiality, including legal requirements. BEA is pursuing a Statistical Production Modernization program which seeks to simplify and modernize processes and tools by first completing business process reengineering and then updating. Accomplishments: Supported the timely, relevant, and accurate release of U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services, April 2023, U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services, Annual Update, Marine Economy Satellite Account, 2021, U.S. International Transactions, 1st Quarter 2023 and Annual Update, U.S. International Investment Position, 1st Quarter 2023 and Annual Update, Gross Domestic Product, 1st Quarter 2023 (Third Estimate), GDP by Industry, and Corporate Profits (Revised), Personal Income and Outlays, May 2023, and Gross Domestic Product by State and Personal Income by State, 1st Quarter 2023. This investment is progressing as expected.

investmentName: Census - Data Ingest and Collection for the Enterprise (DICE)
comment: The Data Ingest and Collection for the Enterprise (DICE) investment continues with implementing a new way of doing business that focuses on minimizing redundancy, lowering complexity, and avoiding duplicative costs for the Census's business and household data ingest and collection operations. DICE continues the efforts of being able to provide a way to collect quality data using one source. The program also continues its efforts to integrate and manage the development of an enterprise system that provides a shared platform for receiving data that has been collected by external sources, census, and survey data. Accomplishments: Closed Program Increment 08 and launched PI-09. Delivered UAT and STAGE environments to the MOJO and Centurion 2.0 development teams. Released QDM production software v3.3 to support the Current Pop Survey. Investment is improving in reporting and is progressing in execution but is operating with a risk exposure.

The Geographic Support Program (GSP) investment supports the integrated and automated computer-based geographic support system crucial to all censuses and household surveys. The investment continues to provide the Census address list, maps, geographic reference files, and processing systems to meet the geographic requirements of all Census Bureau programs and operations. Accomplishments: GSP posted Cartographic Boundary Files.  These boundary files are specifically designed for small scale thematic mapping.  Simplified shapes improve the appearance of geographic areas when displayed at small scales, take up less disk space, and take less time to render on screen.  They are also clipped to a simplified version of the U.S. outline and result in the more iconic recognizable version of the state versus detailed TIGER/Line shapefiles. The investment is progressing with a risk exposure.

investmentName: BEA Estimation Information Technology System (BEA-EITS) for Measuring the Changing US Economy.
comment: The BEA Estimation IT System encompasses BEA's core economic processing system, and directly supports BEA's mission.  This investment supports timely, accurate release of more than 60 critical economic estimates per year. investmentName: Census - Center for Enterprise Dissemination Services and Consumer Information (CEDSCI).
comment: The Program and the CEDSCI EDDE IT Platform project are dedicated to using customer feedback to develop innovative ways to improve customer with improved data and product displays, searches, and downloads accessible from census.gov and on mobile devices. The project is in the development of a modernized platform that disseminates Census data in an efficient technological manner.  The program is responsible for both the development project plus using the new platform for disseminating Census data.  Notable Accomplishments: Completed 100% of program sprints 48 and 47% of program sprint 49.  Released 2 datasets to data.census.gov. The investment still has a risk exposure contributing to the overall rating.

investmentName: OS OFM Commerce Business Applications Solution (BAS) V2
comment: The BAS program continues to modernize the Department's financial management, acquisition, and property systems.  Accomplishments: Sunflower: Completed Sunflower CPU patch. Core Applications: Continued to provide user support for early adopters. Continued planning for training sessions. Data Warehouse: Conducted Contracts Management dashboard demos. The program rating is based on replanning and risks and continues to work through organizational change management risks and challenges to user adoption.

The OS OFM Commerce Business Systems (CBS) investment continues to provide an integrated financial management system that has been implemented throughout the Department of Commerce (DOC) as well as supporting G-Invoicing activities at the bureau level.  Accomplishments: G-Invoicing:  Supporting G-Invoicing activities at bureau level, as well as implementing updates. The investment meets functional requirements. System availability is at 100%. The investment is progressing as expected with minimal risk.

The Patents Product Line investment continues to support the Patents business by creating additional products; retiring/decommissioning more legacy systems; and supporting Patents products operational activities. Notable Accomplishments - Trained 21,846 users to date on filing in DOCX in Patent Center, increasing Patent Center and DOCX usage. Completed 501 Submissions to allow third party users to file prior art submissions. Implemented Angular Next Gen (NG) to improve the Patent Center user interface experience and meet updated government technical requirements. Completed eOffice Action mail and electronic postcard notifications so that customer numbers can be migrated from Private PAIR to Patent Center. Deployed Angular Classification Picture for design and plant examiners. Deployed the latest version of the Classification Allocation Tool and made available to USPTO stakeholders. This deployment focused on rollout of the updated Classification Picture gadget for design and plant examiners to support the retirement of CDS (Classification Data System). The investments is progressing with risks and issues that are being mitigated.

The Trademark Product Line investment continues to maintain all Trademark legacy components across the product line and is in the process of developing modernized business and technical solutions to further improve the delivery of business value. Notable Accomplishments: Successfully deployed EOG Electronic Digital Cert Gold Seal Integration & Queries to comply with USPTO enhanced electronic registration certificates effective April 18th. Deployed Trademark Exam enhancements to enable exam permissions for ExParte Appeal and Madrid 66(a) cases. Deployed 11 TRAM COM services into production via new DevSecOps pipelines as part of the TRAM retirement effort. Deployed TSDR related enhancements for Madrid 66a MP3/MP4 Multimedia submissions. The investment is progressing with some risks and issues that being mitigated.

Enterprise Product Line continues to manage all of the back-office operations including communicating with the public and employees, providing usable data collections and analytics, disseminating public records including assignment records, collecting fees, paying agency bills, supporting legal functions, providing HR capabilities, supporting budget and planning, and managing facilities and assets. Accomplishments: the investment has delivered enhancements to the enterprise financial tools allowing more efficient workflows through component integration for Budget Formulation, Budget Execution, Acquisition Procurement, Activity Based Information and Financial Accounting (Momentum).  These system enhancements and increased automation deliver a greater customer experience for the internal end users and optimize agency performance through budget cycle. The investment is progressing with risks and issues that are being mitigated.

Enterprise Data Lake continues to be a flexible data repository intended to provide the Census Bureau with a next-generation scaling capability to fulfill data storage, reporting, analytics, and security needs while reducing costs associated with duplicative data silos. Notable Accomplishments: Onboarding:  Released Production environment to Human Resource Division (HRD) 2023 Data Science Training Program. Conducted training sessions with HRD users on using EDL. Began provisioning infrastructure for Voice of Customer and Continuous Count Study projects. Completed 3.2 TB and 600 GBs data transfer from IRE to EDL to be used by Demo Frame.  The investment is rated 3 due to risk exposure and reporting concerns.

The Central Processing investment continues to provide increased satellite network bandwidth, processing, and storage capacity. NWS is continuing to work on the impact of COVID-19 on AWIPS NAWIPS schedule and the WCOSS Transition and WCOSS Fee Liability. Accomplishments: NHC transitioned their Sea State product to AWIPS.  AWIPS: Customer Results and Network Availability: 100%; Satellite Master Ground Station Availability: 100%; Met 3 out of 3 performance metrics reported. Rated 3 due to risk profile and issues.

investmentName: NOAA/NESDIS/ Comprehensive Large Array-data Stewardship System (CLASS).
comment: The CLASS program continues to efficiently manage high volumes (petabytes) of satellite and in situ data and automates data ingest, quality control and access.  CLASS is the designated primary archive for most of NOAA environmental data sets. Held data Operational Readiness Review with NCEI to support new processes to send data to CLASS.  Completed decommission of the CLASS node in Boulder, CO. CLASS accomplishments for this month: Successful transition to OMS Task Order Performance metrics: Added 16.48M new catalog files to the archive. Operational Availability - 97.79%. 100% responsiveness to NOAA customers. The investment is executing as expected.

The Geographic Support Program (GSP) investment supports the integrated and automated computer-based geographic support system crucial to all censuses and household surveys. The investment continues to provide the Census address list, maps, geographic reference files, and processing systems to meet the geographic requirements of all Census Bureau programs and operations. Accomplishments: GSP continues to take necessary steps to ensure the U.S. Census Bureau is able to provide the most accurate and updated data. This month GSP completed the Spring 23 Delivery Sequence File.  This includes Master Address File updating and QC Spring DSF Refresh ZIP3 run. These updates allow Census to accurately locate people and places. The investment is progressing as expected.

The Dissemination investment continues to be responsible for promoting increased accessibility, interoperability, and stewardship of NOAA data, leading, delivering, and coordinating NWS contribution to NOAA, DOC, and Administration data dissemination initiatives.  Notable Accomplishments: Completed ISatSS Code Handoff. Began NWSChat 2.0 Pilot in Pacific Region. Conducted Go Live MADIS 4.0. Completed IDP LDM to DISS Production data flow for NWSChat 2.0. The investment is rated a 3 due to the risk profile and issues.

investmentName: BEA Estimation Information Technology System (BEA-EITS) for Measuring the Changing US Economy.
comment: The BEA Estimation IT System encompasses BEA's core economic processing system, and directly supports BEA's mission.  This investment supports timely, accurate release of more than 60 critical economic estimates per year. The BEA-EITS for Measuring the Changing U.S. Economy supports production and dissemination of BEA's critical economic estimates as well as statistical confidentiality, including legal requirements. BEA is pursuing a Statistical Production Modernization program which seeks to simplify and modernize processes and tools by first completing business process reengineering and then updating. Accomplishments: Supported the timely, relevant, and accurate release of seven datasets measuring the U.S. economic activity (U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services, January 2023, Arts and Cultural Production Satellite Account, U.S. and States, 2021, U.S. International Transactions, 4th Quarter and Year 2022, U.S. International Investment Position, 4th Quarter and Year 2022, Gross Domestic Product, 4th Quarter and Year 2022 (Third Estimate), GDP by Industry, and Corporate Profits, Personal Income and Outlays, February 2023, Gross Domestic Product by State and Personal Income by State, 4th Quarter 2022 and Year 2022 (Preliminary). This investment is progressing as expected.

investmentName: Census - Data Ingest and Collection for the Enterprise (DICE)
comment: The Data Ingest and Collection for the Enterprise (DICE) investment continues with implementing a new way of doing business that focuses on minimizing redundancy, lowering complexity, and avoiding duplicative costs for the Census's business and household data ingest and collection operations. DICE continues the efforts of being able to provide a way to collect quality data using one source. The program also continues its efforts to integrate and manage the development of an enterprise system that provides a shared platform for receiving data that has been collected by external sources, census, and survey data. Accomplishments: Release of QDM production software v.3.4 to support AIES and Special Census. Released RISE Tracker sprint 9.1. Data Ingest/RISE Next Generation initial plan and schedule defined.  Investment is improving in reporting and is progressing in execution.

The Economic Censuses and Surveys program is a mixed life cycle investment and continues to support statistical programs that count and profile U.S. businesses and government organizations. ECON investment accomplishments include: The DIPSE Redesign team prepared the UAT baseline documentation for Response Batch Tracking, Change Diaries Search, Data Capture Load Notepad, and Survey Unit Response Data Display.  They also completed Combined Data, Prescreening, and Electronic Workflow Reports.  The team then continued work on Duplicate Review Display and initiated work on Allocate Payments and Payroll.  The Enterprise Data Lake (EDL) was introduced to the AIES/SPACE team, and the team re-imagined the solution based on new EDL requirements which affect data flow. They also ordered and accessed various services from EDL and began work on the initial load of the Business Register (BR) to EDL to SPACE. The PSIP team completed review of item code crosswalks for F-33 (Local Education Agency Finance System) item data.  They also reviewed the data prerequisites for unit level imputation and resolved gaps in prior year(s) item data. The investment is executing as expected.

investmentName: BIS Commerce USXPORTS Exporter Support System (CUESS)
comment: The BIS CUESS investment complements the export enforcement process in support of the single IT System for the Export Control Reform directive. BIS continues to collaborate with other agencies on the USXPORTS system for multi-agency license reviews.  BIS will support the USXPORTS development for release 13.17 that improves the reliability and data efficiencies between CUESS and USXPORTS. BIS and the State Department continue to share data weekly in support of the recommendation from the GAO. Accomplishments Cleaned up duplicate Actions listings in IMS-R. The BIS Automated Export System analytical data from CBP has been updated to the February baseline with 4.4m records. The BIS Consolidated screening list contains data through March 25.   BIS is in the final stages of its Cloud migration effort. The investment is progressing with risks.

The 2030 Decennial investment covers the Design Selection Phase (FYs 2022 - 2024) for the 2030 Census.  The 2030 Census strategic goals are consistent with prior decennial census goals and include: 1) A Complete and Accurate Census, 2) Embraced and Trusted Results, 3) An Efficient and Effective Program, and 4) An Appropriately Sized, Skilled, and Structured Workforce. This investment is currently in the planning phase and is on target to meet all scheduled milestones identified to date.  Accomplishments: Design Selection Phase- Completed IT Strategy and Roadmap.  Completed 2030 Census Risk and Issue Management Plan. The investment is progressing as expected.

The American Community Survey (ACS) Investment continues to support the Bureau's objective of collecting, processing, and releasing information to meet the constitutional and legislative mandates. The American Community Survey has led to a simpler decennial census, provided more timely and relevant data between censuses, and led to widespread efficiencies throughout the federal statistical system. Notable accomplishment: Completed release of ACS 2017-2021 5-year Data Profiles for 2022 State Legislative Districts. Completed submission of ACS 2022 data products package to Disclosure Review Board (DRB) for approval. Completed modification and tested tabulation software applications for ACS 2022 products requirements. Completed review of ACS 2017-2021 5-year SPT/AIAN estimates and update specs if needed. The investment is progressing as expected.

comment: HHS's CIO evaluation is based on the risk evaluation framework provided by OMB's Capital Planning and Investment Control (CPIC) Guidance. As part of HHS's efforts to strengthen implementation of FITARA principles, in August 2017, HHS supplemented its existing CIO evaluation framework to consider the confidentiality and availability of department IT assets as they support public health, confidence and safety of the American people. Application of this additional evaluative factor, and subsequent scoring adjustments, reflects HHS's increased awareness and acknowledgement of risk inherent to investments. As demonstrated by data related to investments' cost, schedule and operations, HHS remains vigilant about establishing internal controls and ensuring strong program/project management to manage and mitigate risk across its IT portfolio.

Centers continue installing the Enhanced AWIPS workstations. Installs anticipated to continue throughout the remaining of  FY2023. HAZARD SERVICES: Completed virtual FAT. Q2 activities include supporting bureau implementation of G-Invoicing mandate. The investment is progressing as expected with minimal risk.

Notable Accomplishments - Trained 20,074 users to date on filing in DOCX in Patent Center, increasing Patent Center and DOCX usage. Deployed Amazon cloud for microservice code changes to support migration from Solr to OpenSearch and defect fixes. Deployed PGPUB OWP Ingestor Module to load positional information so that examiner can view the text positional information on the image viewer. Deployed PCT ST.26 forms and PCT form validation. The investments is progressing with risks and issues that are being mitigated.
